The department structure is intentionally simple: a department may have one parent department, which creates a one-level hierarchy within the same organization. This operation is used by employees who need to inspect the organization structure and by organization managers who need full visibility into department setup. The response should preserve the department's current state and should not alter any employee assignments or hierarchy relationships.

Because department data is organization-scoped, the service must confirm that the requested department belongs to the current organization before returning it. If the department does not exist in the active organization, the operation must reject the request rather than exposing data from another tenant. Deleted departments must not be returned as active department records.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the department by its UUID primary key and restrict the lookup to the current organization context.

Implementation should query the hrm_time_tracking_departments table by id and hrm_time_tracking_organization_id together to guarantee tenant isolation. The service should exclude records marked as deleted_at when presenting active department details, unless the wider application explicitly supports historical department lookup (this endpoint is for active detail retrieval, so deleted records should be treated as unavailable).

If the department exists, map its scalar fields directly and include the parent department reference if available. Because the schema allows only one parent_department_id, no recursive hierarchy traversal is required here. The response should be read-only and should not compute or mutate employee assignments.

Return not found when the department id does not exist in the current organization, and return forbidden when the caller lacks permission to view departments in the selected organization according to the authorization layer. Keep the endpoint free of pagination, filtering, and body payloads.

responseBody.description: Department details for the selected organization.

operations.description:
Update an existing department within the current organization.

This operation allows an organization management user to change the department name, description, and parent department assignment for a department that already belongs to the selected organization. The department is an organizational grouping used to structure employees inside a tenant boundary, and it may optionally reference one parent department to support the organization’s simple one-level hierarchy.

The update is always scoped to the current organization context. The department being updated must belong to that organization, and any parent department assigned during the update must also belong to the same organization. The system must reject attempts to move a department under a department from another organization, or to create a deeper hierarchy than one parent and one child level.

The department name is the primary label used to identify the department within the organization and must remain unique per organization. The department description is optional and may be left empty when no extra context is needed. This operation does not change employee records directly; employee department assignments remain intact unless managed by a separate workflow.

Use this endpoint together with the department detail and department list endpoints to refresh the organizational structure after an update. If the parent department is changed, the client should reload the department tree to reflect the current one-level nesting structure.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target department by id together with its organization scope, then verify that it belongs to the authenticated user's currently selected organization. Reject the request with a not-found or forbidden-style error if the department is outside the active organization context.

Validate the request body fields before saving. The name must be non-empty and must remain unique within the organization. The description is optional and may be null or empty. If parentDepartmentId is provided, load that department and verify it belongs to the same organization. Reject the update if the parent department is the same as the target department, if it belongs to another organization, or if assigning it would violate the one-level hierarchy rule.

Persist only the editable department fields. Do not modify employee records, do not cascade employee reassignment logic here, and do not alter department-created timestamps. Update updated_at automatically as part of persistence. If the application uses audit logging, record the department change as an organization-level activity entry after successful commit.

Handle unique constraint violations on organization-scoped department name gracefully by converting them into a validation error. Return the updated department record after commit so the client can refresh the organization structure immediately.

responseBody.description: The updated department record.

requestBody.description: Department fields to update.

operations.description:
Delete a department from the current organization and clear any employee department assignments that reference it.

This operation removes the selected department from the organization’s internal structure. Departments are organization-scoped records, so the system first verifies that the target department belongs to the currently selected organization before proceeding. If the department belongs to another organization, the request must be rejected.

Deleting a department does not delete employee records. Any employees assigned to the department must remain active, and their department assignment must be cleared as part of the same operation. This preserves employee data while ensuring the removed department no longer appears in organization browsing or management views.

Access is limited to users with organization management permission, because department deletion changes the structure of the organization. Clients commonly perform this operation after loading the department list or department details for the current organization so they can refresh the structure after the deletion is completed.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the target department by departmentId and confirm it belongs to the authenticated user's current organization context. If the department is missing or belongs to a different organization, return a not-found or forbidden-style domain error according to the service error conventions.

Within a single transaction, update every employee record in the same organization that references this department so its department reference becomes null, then delete the department record itself. The employee update and department deletion must be atomic to prevent partially detached organization structure.

Do not touch employees outside the organization context, and do not modify any unrelated employee attributes such as role, status, contract, or project assignments. The business rule is strictly to clear department association while preserving employee records and their active state.

Return the deleted department payload after successful removal so callers can refresh UI state. Ensure authorization checks happen before the transaction and that organization-context validation is enforced again in the persistence layer to avoid cross-organization deletion attempts.

parameters.description: The target department ID within the current organization.
parameters.name: departmentId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of employees for the currently selected organization.

This operation is the main browsing entry point for organization members who need to review the workforce structure, search for specific employees, and filter the list by department, employment type, or current status. The returned records are scoped strictly to the active organization, matching the organization-bound employee membership model stored in the employee table and the one-organization-per-request access boundary described in the domain rules.

The list is built from the organization-specific employee membership records and can surface each employee's current role assignment and optional department placement. The underlying employee record keeps the membership anchored to a single organization, a single linked user account, a single current role, and one optional department, which makes this endpoint suitable for staff browsing and administrative oversight without exposing data from other organizations.

Access to this endpoint is limited to users who have permission to view employees in the active organization. The system must reject requests that attempt to target records outside the current organization context, and it must never mix employees from multiple organizations in one response even if the same user belongs to more than one tenant.

Filtering and search behavior should support organization-level browsing expectations: department filters must only match departments that belong to the active organization, status and employment-type filters must be evaluated against the employee membership record, and the result set should remain empty when no employees match the selected filter combination. Pagination is required because organizations may contain many employees, and the response should return summary information optimized for list views rather than full nested history data.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement an organization-scoped employee search endpoint backed by hrm_time_tracking_employees.

Load only rows whose organization_id matches the active organization context resolved from the authenticated member's selected organization. Reject the request if the context is missing or if the active organization does not authorize employee visibility. Never query across organizations.

Support request-body filters for keyword search, department_id, employment_type, and status. Department filtering must be validated against hrm_time_tracking_departments within the same organization. Search should match the employee's position title and linked user account identity fields available through the user account relationship, but must not expose other-organization data. If the implementation needs employee display name from user profile in the future, it should be joined only through the authenticated organization scope, not by unrestricted global lookup.

Return a paginated page object sorted by the requested sort field or a safe default such as created_at descending. Include current role and department summary data when building each employee list item by joining the current role and optional department references. Because employee role history is stored separately in hrm_time_tracking_employee_roles, only the current employee role should be exposed in the list response, not historical role assignments.

Ensure department filters and any department summary data respect the one-organization boundary. If a department belongs to another organization, treat the request as invalid or return no matches depending on the validation strategy used elsewhere in the service, but never cross-load or cross-join records from outside the active organization.

Use standard pagination validation to clamp page size to the configured maximum and to reject invalid page numbers, malformed search strings, or unsupported sort keys. Map empty results to an empty page response with pagination metadata rather than an error. No transaction is required because this is a read-only search operation.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of employee summaries for the active organization.

requestBody.description: Employee list filters, search criteria, sorting, and pagination options.

operations.description:
Create a new employee membership record for the currently selected organization.

This operation registers an organization-specific employee record that links one global user account to one organization, assigns that employee to a role, and optionally places the employee in a department. The employee table is the core workforce anchor for organization-scoped staffing, role assignment, department placement, and time-tracking ownership, so this endpoint is the starting point for all employee lifecycle workflows.

Only authenticated members with employee management permission in the active organization may call this endpoint. The request is validated against the organization boundary so the referenced user account, role, and department must all be usable within the same organization context. The unique organization-and-user-account constraint is enforced to prevent duplicate employee memberships for the same person inside one organization.

The created employee record is stored with the organization owner, the linked user account, the assigned role, optional department placement, optional position title, employment type, and current status. Clients typically use this endpoint after selecting the active organization context and before navigating to employee detail, role management, department assignment, or time-tracking flows.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implementation should resolve the active organization from the authenticated member context and reject the request if no organization is selected. Verify that the caller has employee management permission in that organization before any database write.

Validate that userAccountId references an existing global user account and that no employee record already exists for the same organization_id and user_account_id pair. Validate that roleId belongs to the same organization; if departmentId is provided, validate that the department also belongs to the same organization. Reject any cross-organization reference.

Persist the employee inside a database transaction. Insert the hrm_time_tracking_employees row with organization_id, user_account_id, role_id, optional department_id, optional position_title, employment_type, and status. Use the schema timestamps as generated by the persistence layer. If invitation linkage is part of the surrounding onboarding flow, that should be handled separately by invitation acceptance logic rather than by this endpoint.

Return the newly created employee with resolved relations needed by client screens, and ensure the service emits an activity record for significant workforce changes if the application layer records employee onboarding events. Handle uniqueness violations, invalid foreign keys, and organization-scope mismatches with clear validation errors.

responseBody.description: The created employee membership record.

requestBody.description: Employee membership details to create in the active organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve the detailed employee membership record for the currently selected organization.

This operation returns one organization-scoped employee record from the employee membership table, which stores the core workforce data used for staffing, role assignment, department placement, and time-tracking ownership. The response is intended for employee detail screens and administrative review, where the caller needs to see the employee’s current organization membership, role, optional department, position title, employment type, status, and account linkage in one place.

The employee record belongs to exactly one organization and must be resolved only within the active organization context. If the requested employee does not belong to the current organization, the request must be rejected. The employee detail view must therefore never leak records from another tenant, even when the same user account belongs to multiple organizations.

This endpoint is read-only and does not change the employee record. It should be used together with the employee list endpoint for browsing and with separate update, deactivate, reactivate, role assignment, and contract endpoints for administrative changes. Any related profile information should be read from the linked user account and user profile relationships for display purposes only, without expanding the scope of this endpoint into a broader search or management operation.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the employee row by primary key and verify that its organization_id matches the currently selected organization context before returning any data.

Use a single read query with joins to the linked user account, current role, and optional department so the detail response can render the employee’s identity and placement without additional round trips. If the implementation uses ORM relations, include the userAccount, role, and department relations in the fetch, but do not include historical employeeRoles rows unless the response schema explicitly requires them.

Validation rules:
- employeeId must be a valid UUID.
- The record must exist.
- The record’s organization_id must equal the active organization id from the authenticated request context.
- The record must not be treated as belonging to another organization even if the account is shared across tenants.

Error handling:
- Return not found when the employee does not exist in the current organization context.
- Return forbidden or not found according to the project’s standard tenant-isolation strategy when organization_id mismatches.

Do not mutate data. Do not load unrelated lists, contract history, timesheets, or timelogs. Keep the operation focused on the current membership snapshot and the minimal linked data needed for a detail page.

responseBody.description: Detailed employee membership information for the selected organization.

operations.description:
Update an employee membership record within the active organization.

This operation edits the organization-scoped employee record that links one global user account to one organization, one role, and an optional department. The employee membership row is the central workforce record for staffing, access assignment, and organization-specific employee lifecycle management, so this endpoint is the standard way to correct an employee's current placement, role, position title, employment type, or active/deactivated state.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to users with employee management permission in the currently selected organization. The system must reject requests that try to modify an employee belonging to another organization, because employee data is isolated by organization boundary and the active organization context governs every employee-scoped action. If the request changes the employee's role, the system must enforce the rule that each employee can hold exactly one role within a given organization by replacing the current active role assignment rather than creating multiple simultaneous roles.

The request may also update department placement, but the chosen department must belong to the same organization as the employee. If the department is changed to null, the employee remains in the organization and simply becomes unassigned from any department. The operation may update the employee's current role assignment and, if the implementation tracks role history, it should record that change in the employee role history table within the same transaction so the historical assignment trail remains consistent.

Validation must ensure that the target employee exists, belongs to the active organization, and that any supplied role or department identifiers also belong to that same organization. The system should also validate status transitions according to the employee lifecycle rules, especially when deactivating or reactivating an employee, and it should reject any update that would violate the one-role-per-employee constraint or other organization membership rules. This endpoint is typically used together with employee detail retrieval, employee listing, and department management operations when administrators reorganize the workforce.
operations.name: putByEmployeeid
operations.specification:
Load the employee record by employeeId and verify it belongs to the currently selected organization context.
Check the authenticated member has employee management permission before any write attempt.
Validate the update payload against the employee update DTO: allow department_id, role_id, position_title, employment_type, and status fields only, with partial updates handled explicitly if the DTO is designed as nullable/optional fields.
If department_id is provided, confirm the department exists and belongs to the same organization; reject cross-organization department references.
If role_id is provided, confirm the role exists and belongs to the same organization; changing the role must preserve the invariant that the employee has exactly one active role in the organization.
If status is changed, apply the organization employee lifecycle rules for active/deactivated transitions and reject invalid state changes.
Persist the employee row update in a transaction. If role_id changes and the system stores role history separately, close the previous active employee role assignment and create a new history row with effective_from set to now, all in the same transaction.
Do not modify user account or profile data here; those belong to separate endpoints.
Return the updated employee aggregate after the transaction commits, including the current role and department references needed by the UI.
Surface standard errors for not found, forbidden, validation failure, and cross-organization access rejection.

responseBody.description: Updated employee membership details.

requestBody.description: Employee membership fields to update.

operations.description:
Delete an employee membership from the currently selected organization.

This operation removes the organization-specific employee record that links a user account to an organization, role, and optional department. The employee entity represents the core workforce membership used for access assignment, staffing, and organization-scoped time tracking. Because the record belongs to one organization and one user account, the server must verify that the target employee is within the active organization context before the deletion is applied.

Only users with organization-level employee management privileges should be able to call this endpoint. The deleted employee may have been assigned a role, department, position title, and employment type, all of which are captured in the underlying employee record. The API must not allow cross-organization deletion attempts, and it must reject requests when the employee does not belong to the current tenant boundary.

The implementation should coordinate with the broader workforce lifecycle rules defined for the platform. Deleting an employee must preserve the integrity of related organization data and should respect any database-level or service-level constraints that protect associated records such as contracts, timesheets, timelogs, or membership links. If the application layer determines that additional preconditions are required, the request must fail cleanly with a validation or conflict response rather than removing the record blindly.

Clients should typically use the employee list or employee detail endpoint before issuing this deletion so they can confirm the correct target and update the UI afterward. The response returns the removed employee record for confirmation and audit-friendly client handling.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Service flow:
1. Resolve the current organization context from the authenticated member session.
2. Load the employee by employeeId with an organization scope check on organization_id.
3. If the employee does not exist in the current organization, return not found.
4. Enforce authorization so only users with organization management or employee management privileges can proceed.
5. Before deletion, verify any required business constraints from the employee lifecycle, including any internal checks for dependent workforce data that would make deletion unsafe.
6. Delete the employee membership record in a transaction.
7. If the delete cascades through related records by database constraint, rely on the configured referential behavior; do not manually invent side effects outside the modeled schema and requirements.
8. Return the deleted employee entity or an equivalent confirmation payload consistent with the platform's delete response pattern.

Implementation notes:
- Use the employee unique scope defined by (organization_id, user_account_id) only as supporting context; the request path uses employeeId, so primary lookup should be by id plus organization scope.
- Do not accept any request body.
- Ensure cross-tenant access is blocked even if the employeeId exists in another organization.
- Emit an organization activity record only if that is part of the existing service pattern for destructive workforce actions.
- Handle concurrent deletion attempts idempotently: a second call against a missing employee in the current organization should return not found.
- Maintain transaction safety so authorization, lookup, and deletion are evaluated against the same organization context.

parameters.description: Employee membership identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Retrieve or manage the contract history for a specific employee within the currently selected organization.

This endpoint works with the employee membership record and its related immutable employment contract history. Each contract stores one employment term with an effective start date, optional end date, pay rate, pay period, expected weekly working hours, and free-form notes. The contract records are preserved as historical business data, so the current active contract and all past contracts remain available for viewing even as a new contract is introduced.

Access to this endpoint follows the employee visibility rules of the organization. An employee may view their own contract history, and users with employee viewing access may view the contract history of any employee in the selected organization context. Creating a new contract or editing the current active contract requires employee management permission. The system must reject any attempt to modify a past contract, because once a contract is no longer active it becomes a historical record and must remain unchanged.

When a new contract is created, the implementation must ensure that only one active contract exists for the employee at any given time. If an active contract already exists, the service must close that current contract by setting its end date to the day before the new contract begins, then create the new contract record inside a single transactional boundary. The employee’s organization boundary must be enforced before any query or write occurs, and the target employee must belong to the current organization.

This endpoint is typically used together with employee detail and employee management operations so the caller can inspect the current contract, review historical contracts, and update the active one when employment terms change. Validation errors should be returned when the employee does not exist in the current organization, when the contract dates overlap incorrectly, when a past contract is targeted for update, or when the caller lacks the required viewing or management permission.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement as an organization-scoped employee contract history endpoint backed by hrm_time_tracking_employees and hrm_time_tracking_employee_contracts.

For read behavior, query contracts by hrm_time_tracking_employee_id using the path employeeId, enforce the current organization context through the employee record, and return contracts ordered by start_date descending so the current active contract appears first. Include current and historical contracts in the response without filtering out inactive records. Do not rely on deleted_at for business logic; the historical record must be returned according to the contract start/end dates and organization membership.

For create behavior, validate that the caller has employee management permission, verify that the employee belongs to the selected organization, and ensure the new contract start_date does not conflict with the existing unique constraint on (hrm_time_tracking_employee_id, start_date). If an active contract exists, wrap the operation in a transaction: close the previous active contract by setting end_date to one day before the new start_date, then insert the new contract with end_date null. Preserve pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, and notes exactly as entered after validating them against business rules.

For update behavior, only allow editing the current active contract. Reject any update where the target contract already has an end_date. When updating the active contract, ensure the resulting dates remain valid and preserve history integrity. Past contracts must be treated as immutable and must not be altered. If date changes are allowed on the active contract, re-check adjacent contract boundaries and prevent overlaps with historical entries.

Authorization rules: allow self-view for the employee’s own contracts and allow any user with employee viewing access to view another employee’s contracts; require employee management permission for create/update mutations. Return 404 when the employee does not belong to the current organization, and return 403 when the caller lacks permission. Use a paginated contract history response so the endpoint can scale for long-running employment histories.

responseBody.description: Paginated employee contract history including the current active contract and past contracts.

operations.description:
Create a new employment contract for a specific employee within the current organization.

This operation stores a contract record as part of the employee’s historical contract timeline and associates it with the employee identified in the path. It is used to record employment terms, keep the employee’s contract history complete, and establish the employee’s current active contract when appropriate.

Only users with employee management permission may perform this action. The request is always evaluated in the currently selected organization context, and the target employee must belong to that organization. The system must reject requests that attempt to create a contract for an employee outside the active organization boundary.

When a new contract is created, the service layer must enforce the active-contract rule: each employee may have at most one active contract at a time. If the new contract becomes the active one, the previous active contract for that employee must be closed according to the business rules before the new record is finalized. Historical contracts remain part of the employee’s contract record and must be returned for viewing operations such as the employee contract history endpoint.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implement this as an employee-scoped contract creation command.

1. Authenticate the caller and require employee management permission.
2. Resolve the current organization context from the authenticated request.
3. Load the target employee by employeeId and verify it belongs to the current organization.
4. Validate the request body against contract creation rules from the contract domain: required employment terms, dates, and status fields must be consistent with the contract model used by the service.
5. Enforce the one-active-contract rule for the target employee. If the incoming contract is marked active or is otherwise the newest open contract, locate the current active contract for the employee and close it before inserting the new one, following the domain rule that only one active contract may exist at a time.
6. Create the new contract row linked to the employee and the organization context.
7. If the business logic defines an automatic end date adjustment for the previous active contract, apply it transactionally so the employee never has two active contracts at once.
8. Return the created contract using the detailed contract response schema.

Use a database transaction for the close-previous-and-create-new sequence to guarantee consistency. Reject the request with a not-found or forbidden error if the employee is outside the selected organization. Reject with a validation error if the request attempts to create an invalid contract state or conflicts with an immutable historical record. Do not allow creation of contracts for employees that are inactive if the contract domain rules disallow it; if the schema or business rules permit it, preserve the employee status checks at the service layer.

This endpoint must not expose editing of past contracts. It only creates a new contract entry and relies on separate read operations for contract history.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single employment contract for an employee within the currently selected organization.

This operation returns one record from the employment contract history maintained for hrm_time_tracking_employees. Each contract stores the effective period, compensation terms, expected weekly working hours, and optional notes for a specific employee. The record is part of the employee’s organization-scoped contract history, and it can represent either the current active contract or a historical contract that has already ended.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to the employee themselves or to a member who has employee viewing access in the current organization context. The system must confirm that the requested employee belongs to the active organization and that the requested contract belongs to that employee before returning the record. If the employee, organization, or contract association does not match, the request must be rejected.

The response includes the immutable contract data stored in hrm_time_tracking_employee_contracts, including the contract period, pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, notes, and audit timestamps. The contract history is preserved for long-term workforce tracking, so this endpoint is read-only and does not modify any contract state. Use the employee-level contract list endpoint to retrieve the full history when needed, and use this endpoint when a client needs the details of one specific contract record.
operations.name: getByEmployeeidAndContractid
operations.specification:
Load the employee contract record by composite scope: employeeId and contractId.

Service flow:
1. Resolve the authenticated member and current organization context.
2. Verify the caller is allowed to view contracts in this organization: either the employee owning the record or a user with employee-view access.
3. Query hrm_time_tracking_employee_contracts by id = contractId and hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = employeeId.
4. Join/verify the related hrm_time_tracking_employees record belongs to the current organization context.
5. If the record is not found, or the employee does not belong to the current organization, return not found to avoid leaking cross-organization data.
6. Return the contract as a single resource object.

Validation and business rules:
- Both employeeId and contractId are UUID path parameters.
- The contract must belong to the requested employee.
- Do not allow access outside the current organization boundary.
- Do not expose any mutation behavior; historical contracts remain immutable.
- The active state is inferred from end_date being null, but this endpoint only returns stored data and does not compute transitions.

Error handling:
- 404 when the contract does not exist for the specified employee or is outside the organization scope.
- 403 when the caller lacks contract viewing access.
- 400 for malformed UUID parameters.

operations.description:
Update an employee contract within the current organization context.

This operation modifies one contract record that belongs to the employee identified in the path. The contract is part of the employee’s historical employment record, and the platform preserves past contracts so the employee’s contract history remains auditable and visible over time. The updated record continues to belong to the same employee and organization boundary; the path parameters establish that scope explicitly.

Only users with employee management permission may perform this operation. The permission model requires employee management access for creating employee contracts and for editing the current active contract of an employee, so this endpoint must enforce that authorization before any data changes are applied. The service must also verify that the target contract belongs to the employee in the path and that the employee belongs to the currently selected organization.

When the updated contract is the active contract, the application layer must preserve the one-active-contract rule for the employee. If business logic allows a new effective start date or updated terms that affect contract continuity, the service must ensure the contract history remains consistent and that the employee does not end up with overlapping active terms. The contract record includes the effective period, pay rate, pay period, weekly working hours, and optional notes, all of which should be validated according to the domain rules and persisted together.

Clients should typically call GET /employees/{employeeId}/contracts/{contractId} before or after this operation when they need to inspect the current contract state. The returned response contains the full contract details, including timestamps, so user interfaces can refresh contract history views immediately after a successful update.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the employee by employeeId within the selected organization and confirm the caller has employee management permission. Then load the contract by contractId and verify it belongs to that employee. Reject the request with a not-found or forbidden-style domain error if the employee-contract relationship is invalid or the employee does not belong to the current organization context.

Apply partial field updates from the request body only to mutable contract attributes: startDate, endDate, payRate, payPeriod, workingHoursPerWeek, and notes. Do not allow the path identifiers to be changed through the payload. Validate date consistency so endDate, when present, does not precede startDate. Validate payRate and workingHoursPerWeek as positive business values, and validate payPeriod against the contract pay-period vocabulary used by the service.

If the contract is the employee’s current active contract, preserve the one-active-contract rule. The update must not create overlapping active periods with other contracts for the same employee. If the application allows adjusting the effective start date, the service must recalculate surrounding contract boundaries only if that behavior is explicitly supported; otherwise, reject a change that would overlap with another contract or make the active contract ambiguous.

Persist the updated contract in a single transaction and return the refreshed contract entity. Update timestamps automatically through the ORM/database layer. No child records are created or deleted by this endpoint, and historical contracts must remain intact. Surface validation errors for invalid dates, invalid pay-period values, unauthorized access, cross-organization access, and employee/contract mismatch.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of roles for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint returns the organization’s full role set, including the fixed built-in roles and any custom roles configured by the organization owner. Roles are always interpreted within the active organization context, so the same role name or capability set in another organization is treated as a separate record.

Built-in roles remain available in every organization and cannot be removed from the role list. Custom roles can be listed alongside them so management interfaces can show the current permission structure, display which roles are already assigned to employees, and support downstream workflows such as editing custom roles or changing an employee’s role assignment.

The response is intended for role administration screens and should be used with organization-scoped authorization. The caller must already have access to the currently selected organization, and the server must reject any attempt to access roles outside that organization boundary. Filtering, pagination, and sorting are handled through the request body so the client can search by role name, separate built-in roles from custom roles, and narrow results to assigned or unassigned roles.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement this as an organization-scoped role search endpoint backed by the hrm_time_tracking_roles table, with an optional join or aggregate lookup against hrm_time_tracking_employee_roles to determine assignment counts or assignment state.

Apply the current organization context from authentication middleware or request context and always filter by organization scope before applying any search criteria. Support pagination in the request body, and allow filters for role name, role kind (built-in vs custom), and assignment state. If the implementation exposes sorting, keep it limited to stable fields such as role name, creation order, or built-in status depending on schema support.

Return a paginated summary collection that includes the role identity, display name, built-in/custom classification, and a compact permission summary where available. Built-in roles must always appear as valid list results even if they are not currently assigned to any employee. Custom roles should be included only if they belong to the active organization.

Reject requests that attempt to reference another organization’s roles, and do not infer cross-organization access from role names. If the schema stores assignment counts indirectly, compute them in a single grouped query or via a separate count subquery to avoid N+1 behavior. Validation errors should cover invalid pagination values, unsupported filters, and any attempt to search outside the current organization context.

responseBody.description: Paginated role summaries for the active organization.

requestBody.description: Role search criteria, pagination, and sorting options.

operations.description:
Create a new custom role within the currently selected organization.

This operation registers an organization-specific access role in the role catalog used by the tenant, and it is intended for organization owners or other users with role management authority. The created role belongs to the active organization boundary and becomes available for employee assignment immediately after creation.

The role record stores the role name, an optional stable internal code, an optional description, a built-in flag, and a display sort order. The built-in roles Owner, Manager, and Employee are system-protected and must not be created through this endpoint. This endpoint is therefore reserved for custom role creation only, while built-in roles remain fixed organization defaults.

If permissions are included in the request, the service must create the corresponding role-permission junction records in the normalized permission mapping table so the role's capabilities are defined by the available permission catalog. Permission identifiers must be validated against the allowed permission set before persistence. The request must not expose organization_id because the current organization context is derived from the authenticated member's selected organization.

Validation must enforce organization-scoped uniqueness for role name and role code. When a duplicate name or code exists in the current organization, the request must fail with a conflict-style validation error. The implementation must also ensure the role is not marked as deleted at creation time and that the final response reflects the persisted role and its assigned permissions.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Resolve the current organization context from the authenticated member session and selected organization; reject the request if no organization context is active.
2. Authorize only organization owners or users with the role-management capability in the current organization.
3. Validate the request body: role name is required, non-empty, and unique within the organization; code is optional but, if provided, must be unique within the organization; description is optional; sortOrder must be a valid integer; builtIn must be false or omitted for this endpoint; permissionIds, if provided, must reference valid permission identifiers from the shared permission catalog.
4. Reject any attempt to create a built-in role or to use reserved built-in identifiers/names for Owner, Manager, or Employee.
5. In a transaction, insert the role row into hrm_time_tracking_roles with organization_id from context, the supplied name/code/description, is_builtin=false, and sort_order from the request.
6. If permissionIds are present, insert one row per permission into hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions using the newly created role id and each permission id; rely on the unique constraint to prevent duplicate permission assignment.
7. Return the created role with its permission collection and minimal organization metadata needed by the UI.
8. On unique violations, return a validation/conflict error that clearly identifies whether the collision was on name or code. On permission mismatch, return a validation error indicating the invalid permission identifiers.
9. Do not allow any cross-organization references or organization_id input from the client; all scoping must come from the authenticated context.

responseBody.description: Created role with its configured permissions.

requestBody.description: Custom role creation details and initial permission selection.

operations.description:
Retrieve the detailed profile of a single organization role by its identifier.

This operation returns one role record from the organization’s role set, including the role name displayed inside the organization, the optional internal code used to recognize built-in roles, the optional human-readable description, the built-in flag, and the display order used when presenting roles in the organization interface. The role data is organization-scoped, so the same identifier must always be resolved inside the currently selected organization context.

The role concept is part of the organization-specific access profile used to classify employees within a single tenant boundary. Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee are protected system roles, while custom roles belong only to the organization that created them. This endpoint must respect that boundary and must not expose a role from another organization even if a matching identifier is guessed.

Access to this endpoint is intended for authenticated members operating within an organization context. The service layer must verify that the requested role belongs to the active organization and reject requests that fall outside that boundary. Related role-permission data is managed by separate APIs and should not be mutated by this endpoint.

This endpoint is commonly used before role editing, employee role assignment, and permission configuration workflows. If the role is built-in, the response can still be retrieved for display, but downstream write operations must preserve the protected behavior defined by the domain rules.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implement a repository lookup against hrm_time_tracking_roles using the requested roleId and the active organization context.

First, validate that the caller is authenticated and has a selected organization context. Then query by id and organization_id together to enforce tenant isolation. If no row is found, return a not-found response rather than leaking whether the role exists in another organization.

Return the role fields from the schema: id, organization_id, name, code, description, is_builtin, sort_order, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The deleted_at column exists in the schema, so the read model may include it for completeness if the system’s read policy exposes deleted records, but the endpoint should normally only resolve active accessible roles based on application rules.

Do not load permissions in this endpoint unless the implementation already has a required role detail composition pattern. If permission data is needed, fetch it through the role-permission relationship in a separate query or dedicated endpoint. Keep the query read-only and avoid transactions.

Edge cases: reject cross-organization access, reject malformed UUIDs at validation time, and return standard not-found or forbidden errors according to auth middleware rules. No request body is needed. Response should be the single role object, not a paginated wrapper.

responseBody.description: Role details for the requested organization role.

operations.description:
Update an organization role within the current tenant context.

This operation allows an authorized organization manager to change the editable properties of a role record that belongs to the selected organization. The role model stores the role name, internal code, description, built-in flag, and sort order, while its capabilities are represented through the role-permission relationship. The API must preserve the tenant boundary defined by the organization and must only resolve the target role within that organization.

The update flow must validate the role's ownership and protection status before applying any changes. A role name must remain unique within the organization, and a role code must remain unique within the organization when present. Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee are permanent organizational role options and their predefined capabilities must not be altered in a way that breaks the standard role model. Custom roles may be edited, but the resulting permission set must use only the permission catalog already available to the system.

When the submitted permission list differs from the current grants, the service should update the role-permission junction rows atomically so the stored permissions match the requested configuration exactly. Because employees hold exactly one role in an organization, the service must also ensure that any role change remains compatible with existing employee assignments and does not attempt to reassign employees implicitly. If the role is currently assigned to employees, the role itself may still be updated if allowed by business rules, but any dangerous changes such as invalid permission codes, duplicate names, or built-in role mutation must be rejected with clear validation errors.
operations.name: putByRoleid
operations.specification:
Resolve the role by roleId and verify it belongs to the current organization context derived from the authenticated member's selected organization. Reject if the role does not exist, is deleted, or belongs to a different organization.

Load the current role together with its existing permissions and validate the incoming update payload. Enforce organization-scoped uniqueness for role name and code: if name or code is changed, check for conflicts among non-deleted roles in the same organization. Reject duplicate names/codes with a conflict error.

If the role is built-in, allow only the fields that the business rules permit for built-in roles. Do not allow changes that would alter the fixed capability set or violate the standard Owner/Manager/Employee protection rules. If the endpoint is intended to support full custom-role editing only, reject attempts to mutate built-in roles entirely. Prefer preserving built-in role immutability except for harmless display fields only when explicitly permitted by the domain rules.

Update the role record inside a transaction. If the request includes permission identifiers, validate every permission against the available permission catalog and replace the role_permission rows for this role atomically: delete grants not present in the request, insert missing grants, and avoid duplicate junction rows. If the request omits permissions, preserve existing grants.

Record updated_at on the role and on affected junction rows as appropriate. Return the updated role with its effective permission set so the client can refresh the edit form. If the role is assigned to employees, do not alter employee assignments; the employees keep exactly one role and retain the updated role reference.

Expected errors: not found for invalid roleId or wrong organization context; conflict for duplicate role name/code; forbidden for unauthorized users; validation error for invalid permission ids or attempts to violate built-in role protection; unprocessable entity when the payload tries to set an inconsistent state.

responseBody.description: The updated role with its effective permissions.

parameters.description: Target role identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: roleId

requestBody.description: Role changes and the desired permission set.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a custom role from the current organization when it is no longer assigned to any employees.

This operation is part of organization role administration and is restricted to the organization owner. The role being removed must belong to the active organization context, because roles are organization-scoped records that define access capabilities inside one tenant boundary. The request targets a single role by its identifier and does not require a request body.

Built-in organization roles are protected and cannot be deleted under any condition. The built-in role set includes Owner, Manager, and Employee. When the target role is a custom role, the system must verify that no employee is currently assigned to it before deletion. If any employee still references the role, the request must be rejected to preserve valid role assignments and avoid leaving staff records without a role.

The deletion should be executed only after the service confirms organization ownership, role ownership within the current organization, and assignment constraints. Related operations typically used before or after this endpoint include listing roles for the organization, viewing role details, and updating employee role assignments so that employees can be moved to a different role before deletion is attempted.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Resolve the active organization context and authenticated actor.
2. Verify the actor is the organization owner; reject with forbidden if not.
3. Load the role by roleId constrained to the current organization.
4. If no role is found, return not found.
5. Check whether the role is built-in; if yes, reject the delete request.
6. Check whether any employee is assigned to the role; if yes, reject the delete request.
7. If the role is custom and unassigned, delete the role record in a transaction.
8. Do not modify employee records implicitly; role reassignment must happen through the employee role update flow before deletion.
9. Emit an activity record if the service uses organization audit logging for role lifecycle actions.
10. Return success with no response body.

Validation and edge cases:
- Role must be scoped to the selected organization; do not allow cross-tenant deletion.
- Built-in roles Owner, Manager, and Employee must always be blocked.
- If the role is referenced by any active employee assignment, fail without partial updates.
- Do not cascade-delete employees or permissions.
- Use a transaction to ensure the role is removed only when all checks pass.

parameters.description: Role identifier within the current organization.
parameters.name: roleId

operations.description:
Update the permission set attached to a role within the current organization.

This endpoint replaces the role's assigned permission bundle with the set provided in the request body. It is used to maintain the access entitlement of a custom role, or to validate that a built-in role remains aligned with its fixed system-defined capabilities. Because roles belong to exactly one organization and permissions are attached through a normalized junction table, the server must resolve the role inside the current organization context before applying any changes.

Only the organization owner may change role permissions. The operation must reject requests that target roles outside the active organization, and it must also reject attempts to alter built-in role capabilities when the request would violate the system-fixed permission set. The role name and permission set together define the business meaning of the role, so the update must be applied transactionally to keep the role and its permissions consistent.

If the request is valid, the server should compare the submitted permission identifiers with the existing role-permission rows, remove obsolete mappings, insert new mappings, and return the updated role with its effective permissions. This operation is intended to be used together with role detail retrieval and employee role assignment endpoints so that administrators can define a role's capabilities before assigning it to employees.
operations.name: updatePermissions
operations.specification:
Load the target role by id and current organization context. Verify that the role belongs to the active organization and that the caller has organization-owner authority for permission management.

Validate that the role exists and is not being accessed across tenant boundaries. For built-in roles, enforce the fixed capability rules from the domain: allow only the system-expected permission bundle and reject any request that attempts to deviate from that bundle. For custom roles, accept the permission list as the authoritative desired state.

Process the update in a transaction: read current role_permissions rows for the role, diff them against the requested permission IDs, delete rows no longer present, insert missing rows, and preserve unchanged rows where possible. Enforce uniqueness of the (role_id, permission_id) pair and validate that every permission id exists in the permission catalog used by the service.

Return the updated role with its permission collection. If the role has employee assignments, do not block permission updates unless the business rules for built-in roles require preservation of fixed capabilities. Emit a role activity record if the application uses audit logging for permission changes.

responseBody.description: The role with its updated effective permissions.

requestBody.description: Desired permission set for the role.

operations.description:
Update the permission set granted to a specific role within the current organization.

This operation manages the role capability set that defines the access entitlement of a role inside one organization. A role belongs to exactly one organization, and each permission represents one business capability such as organization management, employee management, project management, time tracking, approval, reporting, or visibility. The selected permission set becomes the authoritative collection of capabilities associated with the role.

Only the organization owner may use this endpoint to create or adjust custom role permissions. Built-in roles are part of the organization’s system-defined role set, so the request must be validated against role rules before any change is applied. The server must verify that the role exists in the caller’s current organization context, that every requested permission is valid for the platform, and that no duplicate permissions are persisted in the role permission set.

The change must be applied atomically to the role permission association records in hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions. If the requested permission set is meant to replace the current set, the implementation should remove permissions not present in the request and add any newly requested permissions in a single transaction. The response should return the updated role with its effective permissions so clients can immediately reflect the new access entitlement in administration screens.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target role by roleId within the authenticated user's selected organization context.
Verify the role belongs to that organization and reject cross-tenant access.
Check that the caller has organization-owner authority for permission management; do not allow non-owners to modify permission sets.
If the role is built-in, apply the system's role rule checks before modifying permissions. If built-in role permission edits are restricted by business policy, reject the request. If built-in roles are editable in this service, still enforce the canonical permission catalogue and organization scope.

Validate the request body permission list against the platform permission catalogue. Each permission code must exist, must be unique within the request, and must be compatible with the organization's available capabilities. Reject unknown codes and duplicate items.

Perform the update in a transaction:
1) Read existing hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions rows for the role.
2) Compute the desired set from the request body.
3) Delete stale associations not present in the new set.
4) Insert missing associations for new permissions.
5) Return the role with its fresh permission set.

Ensure the operation is idempotent when the same permission set is posted repeatedly. Preserve auditability by emitting an activity record if the system uses activity logging for authorization changes.
Return validation errors for missing role, inaccessible organization, unknown permission codes, duplicate permissions, or insufficient privileges.

responseBody.description: The updated role with its effective permission set.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single permission grant assigned to a role within the current organization.

This operation returns one row from the role-permission association table, which stores the permission capabilities granted to an organization role. In the domain model, a role belongs to exactly one organization and has many permissions, and this endpoint exposes one specific grant record from that role capability set so that administrative clients can inspect the exact permission assigned to the role.

This is a privileged organization-scoped read. The caller must already be operating inside the selected organization context, and the record must belong to the role identified by the path. In the business requirements, only the organization owner can manage custom role permissions, so this endpoint should be protected with the same permission-management access checks used by role editing flows.

The returned data should reflect the normalized association between the role record and the permission catalog entry, including the grant row identifier, the linked role identifier, the linked permission identifier, and timestamp metadata. The implementation should only return an active association record for the specified role and permission grant, and it should reject mismatched organization scope, missing records, or records that no longer belong to the role.

Clients commonly use this endpoint together with the role detail endpoint or the role permissions listing endpoint when reviewing a role capability set before editing it. It is the most precise way to inspect one permission assignment without loading the entire set of permissions for the role.
operations.name: getByRoleidAndRolepermissionid
operations.specification:
Load the permission grant by composite scope: roleId from the path defines the parent role, and rolePermissionId identifies the junction row within that role's permission set. Resolve the role first inside the current organization context, then query hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions by id and hrm_time_tracking_role_id together to ensure the grant belongs to the requested role.

Enforce organization isolation by verifying the role belongs to the selected organization before returning any data. If the role cannot be resolved in the current organization, or if the grant row does not belong to that role, return a not found response to avoid leaking cross-organization identifiers.

Apply active-record behavior for the association row: do not return rows whose deleted_at is set. If the platform uses a standard repository pattern, this should be a simple read-only service method with a single select and no transaction. Join or hydrate the linked permission only if the response contract requires permission metadata; otherwise return the grant row identifiers and timestamps only.

Authorize the request with the same permission-management policy used for role administration. At minimum, require organization owner access for sensitive role-permission inspection. Handle invalid UUID input with validation before database access. No write-side side effects are expected.

responseBody.description: Role permission grant details.

parameters.description: Target role identifier within the current organization.
parameters.name: roleId

operations.description:
Remove a single permission grant from a role inside the current organization.

This operation deletes one record from the role-permission junction data that links a role to a granted permission capability. In the underlying data model, each role belongs to exactly one organization, and each role may have many permission grants through the normalized role-permission table. Deleting this association revokes that specific capability from the role without changing the role itself or the permission catalog entry.

This endpoint is intended for organization owners, because the requirements state that only the organization owner can manage role permissions. The request must target the role and the specific role-permission association so the system can verify that the association belongs to the requested role and that the role is within the current organization context before deletion is performed.

The operation must validate that the role-permission record exists, belongs to the given role, and is not already removed. If the association is not found, the service should return a not-found response. If the authenticated user is not the organization owner, the service must reject the request with a forbidden response. After successful deletion, any authorization checks that depend on the role's permission set should immediately reflect the updated capability set.

This endpoint is typically used together with role listing and role detail operations, where the client first loads the role's current permission set and then removes an unwanted permission grant. Because the role-permission table is normalized, removing this association is the correct way to update access control without rewriting the role or permission entities themselves.
operations.name: erasePermission
operations.specification:
Delete a single hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions row that belongs to the target role.

Implementation steps:
1. Resolve the current organization context from the authenticated member session.
2. Load the role by roleId and verify it belongs to the current organization.
3. Authorize the caller: only organization owners may manage role permissions.
4. Load the role-permission row by rolePermissionId and verify it belongs to the supplied roleId.
5. Ensure the row exists and is not already removed; if missing, return 404.
6. Delete the junction row in a transaction.
7. If downstream permission caching exists, invalidate the role's permission cache after deletion.

Validation and edge cases:
- Reject if the roleId does not belong to the current organization.
- Reject if the rolePermissionId is not attached to the specified role.
- Reject if the caller is not the organization owner.
- Do not delete the role record or the permission record, only the association row.
- No request body is needed because the path identifies the target association.

Data access pattern:
- Read role by id and organization_id.
- Read role permission by id and hrm_time_tracking_role_id.
- Delete by primary key after confirming ownership and linkage.

Return no content on success.

operations.description:
Update the role assigned to a specific employee within the current organization.

Each organization manages its own role set, and this operation applies only inside the selected organization context. The employee must belong to the current organization, and the new role must also belong to that same organization. When the role changes, the system replaces the employee’s existing role assignment so the employee still has exactly one active role in that organization.

This operation supports organization administration workflows where owners or authorized managers reassign employees between the built-in Owner, Manager, and Employee roles or organization-defined custom roles. Built-in roles remain available in every organization, and custom roles are only valid within the organization that created them. If the requested role does not belong to the current organization, the request must be rejected.

The endpoint is commonly used together with employee detail retrieval and role listing operations so the client can present the available role options before submitting the change. The response returns the updated employee role assignment state so the user interface can immediately reflect the new access level.
operations.name: patchByEmployeeid
operations.specification:
Load the target employee by employeeId within the current organization context. Verify the authenticated member has permission to manage organization roles or employee assignments, according to the organization's access rules.

Validate that the employee exists and belongs to the active organization. Load the requested role from the same organization and reject the request if the role is missing or belongs to another organization. Do not allow cross-organization reassignment.

Enforce the one-role-per-employee rule by updating the employee's current role reference in a single transaction. The operation must replace the existing role assignment rather than inserting a second active role assignment. If the schema stores role assignment history separately, close or end the current assignment according to the table's effective-period rules, but ensure there is exactly one active role at completion.

Persist the change and emit any organization activity record required by the system's audit workflow if role changes are tracked. Return the updated employee representation with the new role information. Handle not found, forbidden, and validation errors clearly, especially when the employee or role is outside the current organization or the employee is not allowed to be reassigned.

responseBody.description: Updated employee with the new role assignment.

operations.description:
Assign a role to an employee within the current organization.

This endpoint updates the employee’s organization-specific role assignment so that the employee has exactly one active role in that organization. If the employee already has a role, the new assignment replaces the previous one instead of creating a second role membership. The change applies only inside the currently selected organization and does not affect the same user account in any other organization.

The operation is designed around the organization-scoped employee record described by the platform’s human resources model. An employee belongs to one organization, is linked to one user account, and is assigned one role in that organization at a time. Built-in roles remain fixed capability bundles, while custom roles may be created and managed by the organization owner. This endpoint only performs the employee-to-role assignment step; it does not create roles or modify permission bundles.

Access to this operation should be restricted to users who can manage employees within the current organization, typically the organization owner or a manager with the appropriate employee-management capability. The server must verify that the target role belongs to the same organization as the employee, and must reject any attempt to assign a role from another tenant boundary. Validation should also ensure that the employee exists in the current organization and that the requested role is assignable in that organization.

If the employee already has an active role assignment, the service should update the existing assignment transactionally so the employee ends the request with exactly one role in the organization. The response should return the updated employee view, including the newly effective role, so the client can refresh permissions and display state immediately. Related operations include listing roles for the organization, viewing the employee details, and managing custom role definitions separately.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the target employee by employeeId within the current organization context.
Load the employee record together with its current role assignment.
Resolve the requested role from the same organization only; reject the request if the role does not belong to the current organization or is otherwise unavailable.
Enforce the business rule that one employee can have only one active role in an organization.
If the employee already has a role assignment, update that existing assignment to the new role inside a single transaction rather than inserting a second assignment row.
If the employee has no current assignment record, create the assignment record for the employee and role.

Validate authorization before changing data: require organization-level employee management access, typically owner or manager with employee-management permission.
Validate that the employee belongs to the selected organization context.
Validate that the role belongs to the selected organization context.
If the role is a built-in role, allow assignment but do not alter the built-in permission bundle.
If the role is custom, preserve its existing permissions and only change the employee assignment.

Return the updated employee-role state after commit, including the effective role information needed by the client.
If the employee or role is missing, return a not-found error.
If the request tries to cross organization boundaries, return a forbidden or validation error depending on the API error convention.
If concurrent updates occur, use a transaction or row lock to ensure the employee ends with a single role assignment.

operations.description:
Retrieve the role assignment for a specific employee within the selected organization.

This operation returns the employee-specific role assignment record that represents the employee’s current organizational role. The assignment is interpreted inside the organization boundary, so the same employee may have a different role in another organization without affecting this result. The returned data should include the assignment identity, the linked employee reference, and the linked role information so consumers can understand both the assignment record and the effective role it grants.

The underlying data model follows the organization-scoped employee and role structure: employees belong to one organization, roles belong to one organization, and each employee has exactly one role at a time in that organization. Because of that business rule, this endpoint must validate that the requested employeeRoleId belongs to the employeeId in the path and that both records belong to the same selected organization context before responding.

Access is limited to authenticated members operating within an organization context and subject to organization permission rules for employee and role visibility. The operation is read-only and does not modify the employee’s assignment. If the assignment does not exist, belongs to another employee, or falls outside the active organization context, the service should return a not-found or forbidden-style error consistent with the platform’s standard access rules.

This detail endpoint is commonly used together with employee detail and role management operations. Clients may first load the employee record, then call this endpoint to inspect the current role assignment, or use the organization role list endpoints to compare available roles before changing an assignment elsewhere in the API.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Resolve the selected organization context from the authenticated member request before querying any data.

Fetch the employee role assignment by employeeRoleId and employeeId together, enforcing that the record belongs to the same employee and organization. Use a join or follow-up lookup to load the associated role record so the response can include the role identity and descriptive metadata needed by the client. If the assignment record is not found under the given employee, return a 404-style response.

Validate that the employee exists in the current organization context before returning the assignment. If the employee exists but the role assignment points to a different employee or different organization, treat it as not found for the caller. Do not infer or synthesize a role assignment, because each employee must have exactly one role in an organization and the endpoint is intended to expose the persisted record only.

No transaction is required because this is a read-only operation. No pagination, search, or sorting is needed. Do not include mutating fields or role-permission editing behavior. If the system exposes permission details on the role entity, include them through the role relation rather than by expanding unrelated employee data. Ensure the response schema is a single-object detail type, not a page or summary list.
