operations.description:
Update the role assignment for a specific employee within the current organization.

This operation changes which organization-scoped role is active for the target employee while preserving the rule that each employee has exactly one role in that organization. The employee record is the core workforce membership entry for an organization, and the role reference on that record must always remain aligned with the employee's current access level inside the tenant boundary.

The service must verify that the employee belongs to the currently selected organization and that the replacement role also belongs to the same organization. The organization-specific role set is isolated per tenant, so a role from another organization must be rejected. Built-in roles remain fixed choices and custom roles may only be assigned when they already exist in the organization's role set.

Implementation should treat this as a role transition rather than a simple field overwrite. The current active role assignment should be ended, and a new effective role assignment should be created so the system preserves role history for auditing and future reporting. The update must not create a second active role for the same employee, and it must not move the employee across organizations or alter unrelated employee profile fields such as department, position title, or employment type.

Use this operation together with employee detail retrieval and role listing operations when the client needs to present valid role choices before submitting the change. If the employee or role does not belong to the current organization, or if the request attempts to violate the one-role-per-employee rule, the service must reject the request with a validation error.
operations.name: putByEmployeeidAndEmployeeroleid
operations.specification:
Load the employee by employeeId and ensure it belongs to the current organization context. Load the target role by employeeRoleId and verify that it is a valid role record within the same organization as the employee. Reject the request if either record is missing or cross-organization.

Determine whether the employee already has an active role assignment. End the current active assignment by setting its effective_to to the new assignment start timestamp, then create a new hrm_time_tracking_employee_roles record with the employee id, the chosen role id, effective_from as now, and effective_to as null. Because the employee schema also stores a current role_id, update that field to the new role in the same transaction so the employee record always reflects the active role.

Keep the operation transactional to avoid leaving the employee with zero or multiple active roles. If the current role is already the same as the requested role, either no-op safely or return the current employee representation without duplicating history, depending on service conventions, but do not create a duplicate assignment row.

Validate organization scope before writing, since both employee and role are organization-bound. Do not allow changing department, position title, employment type, or user account link through this endpoint. Return the updated employee with its current role relation populated so clients can refresh the UI after the change.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of projects that belong to the currently selected organization.

This endpoint is the primary browsing surface for project records within the organization context. It allows clients to search and filter the organization’s project catalog, especially by project status, so users can distinguish active work from archived or completed historical records. The response is optimized for list displays and does not return the full project detail payload for every item.

Access to this endpoint is limited to authenticated members who have project viewing capabilities in the current organization. The returned projects must be scoped strictly to the active organization context; projects from any other organization must never appear in the result set. This is especially important because the system supports multi-tenant organizations and the same member may belong to multiple organizations.

The request body is used for pagination, optional sorting, and status-based filtering. The status filter must accept only project statuses supported by the system, and the backend must apply the filter before paginating results. If no projects match the selected status, the endpoint should still return a valid empty page response.

This browsing endpoint is commonly used together with project detail retrieval, project editing, project archiving/completion, and assigned-project views. Users who manage projects may use the same endpoint to review the full project list before performing updates, while regular members use it to find projects they can view or are assigned to.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a paginated project search service over the hrm_time_tracking_projects table, always constrained by the authenticated member's selected organization context.

Apply organization_id filtering first, then status filtering, then any additional search/sort criteria, and finally pagination. The status filter must only accept supported project statuses and should reject unknown values during validation. Use a stable ordering for pagination, with explicit sort support if the request DTO includes it.

Return a summary page DTO containing pagination metadata and project summaries. The summary projection should include only fields suitable for browsing, such as identifiers, name, status, schedule dates, color/display metadata, and budget-related values if present in the schema. Do not include write-only or sensitive fields that are not required for list browsing.

Enforce authorization by verifying the caller has access to the current organization and project-view capability. If the caller lacks permission, return a forbidden response. If the organization context is missing or invalid, reject the request before querying data.

Ensure the query never leaks cross-organization records. If the request attempts to filter by an invalid status or malformed pagination input, return a validation error. If the result set is empty, return an empty page object with correct pagination metadata rather than an error.

This endpoint must be read-only and must not modify project records. It should be implemented as a repository/service query with indexes on organization and status fields if available, and should be reusable by both general project browsing and assigned-project UI flows.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project summaries for the current organization.

requestBody.description: Pagination, search, sorting, and status filter criteria for browsing projects.

operations.description:
Create a new project in the currently selected organization.

This operation creates the organization-owned work container used for planning, assignment, time tracking, and delivery tracking. A project belongs to exactly one organization, so the authenticated user must already be operating within an organization context before this request is accepted. The resulting record is isolated to that tenant boundary and will appear in project browsing, project detail, task management, and time tracking workflows for that organization only.

Users with project management permission can use this endpoint to register a new project with its display name, optional description, required color code, optional budget hours, and optional schedule dates. The project status is initialized through the request body to support the lifecycle states recognized by the system: active, archived, and completed. Status changes are handled later by update operations, while this creation endpoint focuses on establishing the new project identity and metadata.

The project record is stored in the organization project table, which carries the project identity, visual recognition color, lifecycle status, budget hours, start date, and end date. Employee assignment is intentionally not part of this operation because project membership is represented in the separate project membership table. After creation, the project can be assigned members, used for task creation, and referenced by timelogs once it is active.

Validation must ensure that the project name is acceptable within the current organization, the color code is present, and any provided dates and budget values are coherent. The service layer should also enforce that the authenticated user has project management permission in the selected organization context. If the organization context is missing or the caller lacks permission, the request must be rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implement this as an organization-scoped project creation workflow in the project service.

1. Resolve the authenticated member and selected organization context from the request context.
2. Verify the caller has project management permission in the current organization.
3. Validate the incoming payload against the project create DTO:
   - name: required, trimmed, non-empty
   - description: optional
   - colorCode: required
   - status: required and limited to active, archived, or completed
   - budgetHours: optional numeric value
   - startDate/endDate: optional dates, with endDate not earlier than startDate when both are provided
4. Check uniqueness of the project name within the organization using the composite unique constraint on organization_id + name.
5. Create the project row with the current organization_id and timestamps.
6. Do not create memberships, tasks, or timelogs here; those are separate workflows.
7. Optionally emit an activity record in the application layer after successful creation if the system’s activity logging flow is enabled for project creation events.
8. Return the created project as the response payload.

Handle conflicts with a duplicate-name validation error mapped from the unique constraint. Reject the request if the organization context is absent, if the user lacks permission, or if date/budget validation fails. Keep the operation strictly within the selected organization boundary; never accept an organization identifier in the payload for this endpoint.

responseBody.description: The newly created project record.

requestBody.description: Project creation data for the selected organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve the detailed information for a single project in the currently selected organization.

This endpoint returns one project owned by the active tenant boundary, including the project name, optional description, required display color, lifecycle status, optional budget hours, and optional start and end dates. The data comes from the project record itself and is intended for project detail screens, edit forms, and historical review of active, archived, and completed projects.

Access is limited to authenticated members who can view projects in the current organization context. Project viewing access must not cross organization boundaries, and the project identifier is resolved only within the organization that the caller has selected. Members with project management access can use the same endpoint to inspect records before updating, archiving, completing, or deleting them through other project operations.

The response reflects the underlying project storage model, including the organization owner reference, human-readable name, visual color code, lifecycle state, planned budget hours, and schedule dates. Validation and lifecycle rules such as preventing new timelogs on archived or completed projects are enforced by the appropriate write operations, while this endpoint simply exposes the current state so that clients can apply the correct behavior.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load a single hrm_time_tracking_projects record by id with tenant scoping.

Implementation steps:
1. Resolve the active organization context from the authenticated member request context.
2. Query hrm_time_tracking_projects by id = :projectId and organization_id = activeOrganizationId.
3. Exclude any record whose deleted_at is not null, because the project is no longer active for browsing and detail access.
4. If no row is found, return a not-found response rather than revealing whether the id exists in another organization.
5. Check the caller has project viewing access in the active organization; project management permission also qualifies.
6. Return the full project DTO with id, organizationId, name, description, colorCode, status, budgetHours, startDate, endDate, createdAt, and updatedAt.

Do not join project memberships, tasks, or timelogs in this endpoint. Those are separate resources and would increase payload size unnecessarily. Keep the query read-only and lightweight. Ensure the service normalizes date-time fields to ISO 8601 in UTC and preserves nullable fields as null when absent.

responseBody.description: Detailed project information.

parameters.description: Target project ID within the active organization.
parameters.name: projectId

operations.description:
Update the project record for the currently selected organization.

This operation allows authorized project management users to edit an existing project’s core identity and planning metadata, including the project name, description, color code, lifecycle status, budget hours, start date, and end date. The project belongs to a single organization, so the update is always resolved within the active organization context and must not affect projects in any other tenant.

The project entity stores the organization ownership, human-readable name, optional summary, display color, lifecycle status, planned budget hours, schedule dates, and audit timestamps. The API must preserve the project’s identity while applying only the allowed editable fields. The `status` field controls whether the project is active, archived, or completed, and the service layer must enforce the business rules that archived and completed projects remain historical records while still being visible to authorized users.

Only users with project management permission may perform this update. The service must verify that the target project belongs to the current organization context before applying changes. When the name is changed, the service must enforce the organization-scoped uniqueness constraint on project name. When the status changes, the service must validate lifecycle transitions and ensure any downstream rules tied to archived or completed projects remain intact, including the restriction that no new timelogs may be created for those states.

This operation is commonly used together with the project list and project detail endpoints. Clients typically call the project detail endpoint first to load the current project state, then submit this update request, and finally refresh the project detail or list view to reflect the new values.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Resolve the project by projectId within the authenticated user's selected organization context.
Validate that the caller has project management permission before any data mutation.

Load the project by primary key and confirm organization_id matches the selected organization. If not found in the current organization, return a not-found response.

Apply updates to the mutable fields only: name, description, color_code, status, budget_hours, start_date, and end_date. Do not allow organization_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, or id to be modified by the client.

When name changes, enforce the unique constraint on (organization_id, name). When status changes, accept only the lifecycle values defined by the project domain and ensure archived/completed state transitions are valid. Keep historical project records accessible after status changes, and do not touch related timelog rows in this operation.

If the project is already archived or completed, allow metadata edits only if the business rules permit them, but preserve the restriction that no new timelogs can be created for that project state. This endpoint must not manage memberships, tasks, or timelogs.

Persist the update in a single transaction and return the updated project entity. If any validation fails, surface a clear domain error describing the violated rule.

responseBody.description: The updated project record.

requestBody.description: Project fields to update.

operations.description:
Permanently deletes a project from the currently selected organization.

This operation removes a single project resource when the caller has project management access and the project belongs to the active organization context. The deletion is only permitted when the project has no timelogs associated with it, because recorded work history must remain available and must not be erased as part of project removal.

The service must first resolve the project within the caller’s organization boundary, then verify that no timelog records reference that project. If any timelogs exist, the request must be rejected and no data must be removed. This rule applies regardless of whether the project is archived or completed, because status changes do not alter preservation requirements for tracked work history.

This endpoint is typically used after a project is no longer needed and has not accumulated tracked time. Related project lifecycle operations such as archiving or completing a project should be used when the project should remain available for historical visibility instead of being removed entirely.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Resolve the target project by projectId within the current organization context.
Authorize the caller using the project management permission.
Check whether any timelog records exist for the project. If at least one timelog is found, reject the operation with a domain validation error and do not delete anything.
If no timelogs exist, delete the project record in a single transaction. Also remove any project-scoped association records that depend on the project and are allowed to be deleted by cascade or explicit cleanup rules, but do not affect timelogs because deletion is blocked before that point.
Return the deleted project representation after successful removal.
Handle not-found and cross-organization access as a standard resource lookup failure. Do not expose project deletion for users without project management permission.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of tasks for a specific project.

This operation returns the tasks that belong to the project identified by the `projectId` path parameter. It is intended for task browsing, filtering, and search within the current organization context, and it respects the project visibility rules defined by the system. Employees can only see tasks in projects they are assigned to, while project leads and users with project management permission may manage tasks according to their broader project access rights.

The returned data is optimized for list views and task boards. It should include summary information such as task identity, title, status, priority, assignment, and due-date related metadata, but it should not return the full task record or task history. Filtering by task status must be honored when present, and additional filters such as priority, assignee, and text search should be applied together without changing the underlying task data.

Because tasks are always owned by a project, this endpoint depends on the project context already being resolved. The server must verify that the authenticated member is allowed to access the project before querying tasks. If the caller does not have access to the project, the response should be an empty paginated result for normal visibility rules or an authorization error when the project itself is not accessible in the current organization context.

This endpoint is commonly used together with task detail retrieval, task status updates, and task history views. When a task status changes through other task operations, those changes should appear in the related task history entries, while this list endpoint continues to reflect the latest task state for the project.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a project-scoped task search endpoint using the tasks table filtered by the target project identifier. Validate that the `projectId` exists in the current organization context and that the authenticated member has access to the project through project membership or project management permission. If the caller lacks access to the project, reject the request according to the authorization policy for project-scoped resources.

Build a query against hrm_time_tracking_tasks using the project foreign key as the mandatory base predicate. Apply optional filters from the request body for status, priority, assignee, due date range, and text search. Honor status filtering exactly as requested; when no rows match, return an empty page rather than an error. Support stable ordering for list browsing, such as due date, priority, and creation order, and make the ordering deterministic for pagination.

Return a paginated summary projection of tasks only. Do not include task history records or unrelated project metadata in the collection payload. The response page should include pagination metadata and a `data` array of task summaries. Ensure that task visibility is evaluated against the current organization and project membership rules before returning any row. If the caller is a project lead, allow project-scoped management visibility; if the caller has project management permission, allow broader task management visibility within the organization, but still keep the project as the top-level scope.

Do not mutate task records in this operation. Do not move tasks between projects. Do not change statuses or assignment data as part of filtering. If the request body includes filters that conflict with each other, combine them with AND semantics unless the filter definition explicitly requires otherwise. Any invalid filter values should be rejected with validation errors before query execution.

Use the response type as a page wrapper for task summaries. The page contract should match the platform's standard pagination structure used for other list endpoints.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of task summaries for the selected project.

parameters.description: Project identifier within the current organization.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for project tasks.

operations.description:
Create a new task within the specified project.

This operation creates a task record that belongs to exactly one project and becomes part of that project’s work queue. The task stores its title, optional description, workflow status, priority, optional estimated hours, and optional due date, matching the task model used for project delivery tracking. If a parent task is provided, it must belong to the same project and represents one-level task nesting only.

Task creation is controlled by project access rules. A project lead may create tasks only in the project where that employee holds the project-lead role, while users with project management permission may create tasks within their authorized organization context. The system must also ensure that the assigned employee, when provided, is a member of the same project through the project membership table. This endpoint is intended to be used together with project membership and project detail retrieval so the client can confirm scope, available assignees, and current project state before creating the task.

The project identified by the path parameter defines the task’s tenant boundary and visibility scope. Tasks cannot be created outside a project, and the request must be rejected if the project is archived or completed, because those states do not accept new work items. The operation should also validate that the project exists, belongs to the current organization context, and is accessible to the authenticated member. Any task history is created separately when task status later changes; this endpoint only creates the current task record.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the target project by projectId within the authenticated member's selected organization context.
Verify the project exists, is not deleted, and is not archived or completed before allowing task creation.
Authorize the caller by checking either project-lead membership for that exact project or organization project management permission.

Validate request body fields against the task schema and business rules:
- title is required and must be persisted as the task title
- description is optional
- status is required or defaulted according to the task lifecycle policy used by the service, typically open
- priority is required because the database model stores it as mandatory
- estimatedHours is optional and maps to estimated_hours
- dueDate is optional and maps to due_date
- assignedEmployeeId, if provided by the DTO design, must reference an employee who is a member of the same project
- parentTaskId, if provided, must reference a task in the same project and must not create deeper than one-level nesting

Persist the task in a transaction, ensuring the project foreign key is set from the path rather than from the client payload. If assignment validation fails, return a domain validation error. If the parent task belongs to another project or would create an invalid hierarchy, reject the request. If the project is archived or completed, reject the request with a business-rule error.

After insert, return the created task with its generated identifier and core fields. If the service emits activity records for task creation, do so in the same transaction only if the application already uses activity logging for project work events.

responseBody.description: The created task record.

requestBody.description: Task creation payload for the specified project.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single task that belongs to a specific project within the current organization context.

This endpoint returns the authoritative task record for one task inside one project. A task is always owned by exactly one project, and the task detail response should reflect that relationship together with the task's title, description, workflow status, priority, optional assignee, optional parent task, estimated hours, due date, and audit timestamps. The project relationship is essential because task visibility and access are always evaluated in the context of the project that owns the task.

Access to this endpoint is restricted by project visibility rules. An employee can view the task only when they are assigned to the project that owns it, while users with project management permission may access tasks according to their broader organization-level project access rules. The service must verify that the requested task actually belongs to the requested project and must reject mismatched or cross-project identifiers, even if both records exist independently.

This operation is typically used by task detail pages and task side panels after the caller has already loaded the project context. If the caller does not have access to the project, the service must respond as if the task is not visible. The endpoint does not modify task state and does not require any request body.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the task by matching both the project identifier and the task identifier in a single query. Enforce tenant isolation by resolving the current organization context first, then ensuring the target project belongs to that organization before fetching the task.

Query the task table with a predicate on task.id = taskId and task.hrm_time_tracking_project_id = projectId. Join or separately verify the owning project record to confirm it belongs to the caller's organization and is not outside the current organization boundary. If the project is archived or completed, the task may still be readable, so only block access when the caller lacks project visibility or the task-project relationship is invalid.

Apply authorization checks before returning data: the caller must be a member with access to the project, or hold project management permission that grants broader project visibility. If the caller is only permitted to view assigned projects, verify they are assigned to the project via the project membership table. If the task is not accessible, return a not-found style response rather than leaking the record's existence.

Return the full task detail schema populated from the task record, including project reference, assignee reference if present, parent task reference if present, title, description, status, priority, estimated hours, due date, createdAt, and updatedAt. Do not include any write-only or derived fields that are not part of the task entity. No transaction is required because this is a read-only operation. Handle missing records, cross-project mismatches, and organization mismatch as standard not-found or forbidden cases according to the application's error policy.

responseBody.description: Task details for the requested project task.

parameters.description: Project identifier that scopes the task.
parameters.name: projectId

operations.description:
Update a task within a specific project.

This operation modifies a single task that belongs to the project identified by the path. It is intended for editing task details while preserving the task's project ownership and visibility rules. A task cannot be moved outside its project context through this endpoint, and any assignment change must keep the task assigned to a valid project member.

Access is controlled by project-scoped permissions. A user with project management permission can update tasks within the organization context they are working in, while a project lead can update tasks only in the project they lead. Employees can only work with tasks in projects they are assigned to, so the service must verify project membership before allowing task updates that would expose or reassign work outside the user's access boundary.

When task status changes, the system must create a corresponding task history entry so the progression of work remains traceable. The update flow should validate any parent-task relationship, confirm that the parent belongs to the same project and does not violate the one-level nesting rule, and ensure that the assigned employee is a current member of the same project. If the task is updated successfully, the API returns the refreshed task record reflecting the latest state.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement as a project-scoped task update endpoint.

1. Resolve the project by projectId and confirm the authenticated member has access to the project. Accept either project management permission or project-lead rights for that project.
2. Resolve the task by taskId within the same projectId. If the task does not belong to the given project, return a not-found response to avoid cross-project leakage.
3. Parse the request body as an update DTO for editable task fields only. Do not allow projectId or taskId to be changed via the body.
4. Validate business rules before writing:
   - If assignedEmployeeId is provided, confirm the employee is assigned to the same project through ProjectMembership.
   - If parentTaskId is provided, confirm it exists in the same project, is not the task itself, and does not create nesting beyond one level.
   - If status changes, ensure the transition is allowed by task workflow rules from the loaded requirements.
   - Preserve task visibility restrictions; do not broaden access through the update.
5. Execute the update in a transaction.
   - Update the task row.
   - If the status changed, insert a TaskHistory record capturing previous status, new status, acting user, and timestamp according to the schema fields available.
6. Return the updated task after reloading it with any related display fields required by the task response schema.

Error handling:
- 403 when the caller lacks project-lead/project-management authority for the target project.
- 404 when the project or task cannot be resolved in the given project scope.
- 409 or 422 when assignment, nesting, or status-transition rules are violated.
- 400 for malformed identifiers or invalid payload structure.

responseBody.description: Updated task details

requestBody.description: Task fields to update

prerequisites.description: A task record must exist within the target project before it can be updated, and creating the task in the same project scope provides the taskId used by this endpoint.

operations.description:
Delete a task from a project.

This operation permanently removes a task that belongs to the specified project and organization context. Tasks are project-scoped work items, so the task can only be deleted when the caller identifies both the project and the task, ensuring the resource is addressed within the correct project boundary.

Access to this operation is restricted to users who can manage project work in the current organization context. That includes a project lead for the target project and users with project management permission. The deletion request must be rejected if the task does not belong to the provided project, if the caller does not have sufficient access, or if the task is still protected by business constraints that prevent removal.

The task domain is tightly connected to project execution and historical traceability. Because tasks may be referenced by project workflows and time tracking activity, the service layer must verify all dependency rules before deletion and fail with a validation error when the task cannot be safely removed. If deletion is allowed, the task is removed from project records and the deleted task payload is returned so clients can reconcile their state.

Related operations include listing tasks within a project, retrieving task details, updating task status, and viewing task history. Clients should typically confirm the task is no longer needed before invoking this endpoint, especially when the task is already part of active work tracking or reporting workflows.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement a project-scoped task deletion handler.

1. Resolve the current organization context from the authenticated member and ensure the caller is acting inside that organization.
2. Load the target project by projectId within the organization boundary.
3. Load the task by taskId and verify it belongs to the resolved project.
4. Authorize the caller using project-lead membership for the project or organization-level project management permission.
5. Before deleting, validate business constraints that would make the task non-removable. In particular, reject deletion if the task is protected by any existing references that the domain does not allow to be broken. Preserve history integrity and do not remove any task history records unless the domain explicitly permits cascading removal.
6. Perform the deletion in a transaction so the task lookup, validation, and removal remain consistent.
7. Return the deleted task payload after successful removal.

Error handling:
- Return 404 when the project or task cannot be found in the current organization/project scope.
- Return 403 when the caller lacks project lead authority or project management permission.
- Return 409 or a validation error when business rules prevent deletion because of linked work history or other protected references.

Do not accept a request body. The path parameters are sufficient for identification and scoping.

parameters.description: Target task's ID within the project.
parameters.name: taskId

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of finalized timelog records for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint is designed for browsing work entries that belong to the organization-specific employee time tracking ledger. Each timelog stores the organization that owns the record, the employee who logged the work, the project that was worked on, an optional task reference, the date context for the work, the recorded duration, a short work description, and whether the entry is billable. The list view is intended to power organization dashboards, employee time reviews, project time inspection, and weekly reporting screens.

Access to this endpoint is governed by the caller’s organization context and time visibility permissions. By default, a member should only see their own timelogs within the selected organization. Users with broader time visibility or time management capability may query other employees’ timelogs in the same organization. The system must always enforce organization isolation so records from another tenant can never appear, even if the search criteria would otherwise match.

The response preserves historical records for projects whose status is archived or completed. Those projects are not allowed to receive new time entries, but existing timelogs remain available for browsing and reporting. This endpoint therefore serves as the read side of the time tracking workflow, complementing the create, update, delete, timesheet, and timer operations that manage how timelogs are produced and locked.

Filtering should support work date ranges, employee, project, optional task, and billable state. Sorting should support common review and reporting orders such as newest first by work date or creation timestamp. Pagination must be stable and deterministic so users can page through large result sets without losing consistency between requests.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a paginated search query over hrm_time_tracking_timelogs scoped to the authenticated organization.

Resolve the active organization from the request context and reject access when no organization is selected. If the caller lacks org-wide time visibility, automatically constrain the search to the caller’s employee record and ignore any broader employee filter that would expose other employees’ timelogs.

Build a filtered query using the request body criteria: work date range, employee_id, project_id, task_id, billable flag, and optional free-text matching against description if supported by the search DTO. Exclude records outside the organization boundary and apply the schema’s deleted_at semantics consistently with the application’s browsing policy. The query should sort deterministically, defaulting to work_date desc and id desc for tie-breaking unless the request specifies another allowed sort order.

Return a page container with summary items only. Include the core fields needed for list views: id, employee, project, task, work_date, duration_minutes, billable, description preview, and timestamps. Do not hydrate unrelated graphs or timesheet membership arrays. If a requested project is archived or completed, still include its historical timelogs because the business rules explicitly preserve them.

Validate that employee_id, project_id, and task_id, when provided, all belong to the same organization. If task_id is present, ensure it belongs to the specified project and organization. Return a standard validation error for malformed filters and an authorization error for attempts to browse outside the caller’s allowed scope.

responseBody.description: Paginated timelog summaries for the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for timelog browsing.

operations.description:
Create a new time entry for the authenticated employee in the currently selected organization.

This operation records work performed on a specific project as a timelog, with an optional task association and a free-form work description. The timelog is owned by the employee who submits it and is always stored within the active organization context, so clients must not attempt to supply employee ownership or organization membership directly.

The underlying timelog record represents the finalized employee time entry used throughout the time-tracking workflow. It may later be included in a draft timesheet, reviewed in a submitted timesheet, or locked when an approved timesheet contains it. Because of that lifecycle, the service must validate that the selected project belongs to the current organization, and if a task is provided, that task must also belong to the same project.

Only authenticated members acting within their selected organization context may call this endpoint. The service must reject attempts to create entries for another employee, to reference a project outside the organization, or to attach a task that does not belong to the chosen project. The endpoint is intended for employee self-entry, not for organization-wide time management or administrative imports.

Successful creation should return the full created timelog so the client can immediately show the saved work entry and use it in later draft-timesheet workflows. If the organization or project context is invalid, or if the supplied duration/date data violates business rules, the request must fail with a validation error rather than creating a partial record.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implement as a self-service timelog creation command in the time-tracking service.

Load the authenticated member and the currently selected organization from the request context. Derive employee ownership from that context; do not accept employee identity or organization identity from the payload. Validate that the caller has a valid employee record in the selected organization and that the employee is allowed to create personal timelogs.

Validate the request body fields against business rules before inserting the record:
- project must exist and belong to the selected organization
- optional task, if provided, must exist and belong to the same project
- work date must be a valid date within the organization’s operational rules
- duration must be positive and within supported granularity
- billable flag, if supported by the schema, should be stored as provided
- description, if present, should be trimmed and length-checked

Perform the insert in a single transaction. Resolve project and task ownership first, then create the timelog with the authenticated employee as owner and the current organization as scope. If the database schema includes any computed or audit fields, let the persistence layer set them. Do not allow cross-organization references. If the project is archived, completed, or otherwise disallowed for new time entries, reject the request with a business validation error.

After insertion, return the created timelog entity. If the implementation emits activity records or downstream events for significant time-entry actions, do so after the insert succeeds, but keep the API response centered on the created timelog. Handle not-found, forbidden, and invalid-reference cases explicitly with clear error mapping.

responseBody.description: The created timelog record.

requestBody.description: Time entry details for the authenticated employee.

prerequisites.description: A project must be created and exist in the current organization before a timelog can reference it; otherwise the timelog cannot be attached to a valid project context.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single finalized time entry by its timelog identifier.

This operation returns one employee timelog record from the currently selected organization context. The timelog represents a worked time entry that belongs to one organization, one employee, and one project, with an optional task reference when the work was tied to a specific task. The returned record includes the work date, duration in minutes, optional description, billable flag, and creation/update timestamps so the client can display the full time entry details without making any additional lookup calls.

Access to this endpoint is limited to the timelog owner and to users who have organization-wide visibility over timelogs in the selected organization. A member without broader visibility can only retrieve their own timelogs. The application must verify that the requested timelog belongs to the active organization context before returning it, because the same authenticated user may belong to more than one organization.

The endpoint reads the underlying hrm_time_tracking_timelogs record directly and must not return entries that are no longer available for viewing. The response should include the linked organization, employee, project, and optional task relationship identifiers as part of the main timelog representation so the consumer can render a complete detail view and safely use the result for review or follow-up editing workflows.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the timelog by primary key UUID and join or hydrate the organization, employee, project, and optional task references needed for the detail response.

Before returning data, confirm that the timelog belongs to the currently selected organization context. If the authenticated member does not have organization-wide timelog visibility, also confirm that the employee_id on the record matches the current member's employee identity in the organization. If either check fails, return a not-found or forbidden response according to the platform's authorization conventions.

Use a single read query with organization scoping to avoid cross-tenant leakage. The query should exclude records marked as deleted_at if the platform treats deleted records as non-retrievable from the API.

No transaction is required because this is read-only. Include error handling for invalid UUID format, missing timelog, and unauthorized access. Return the full domain object type rather than a summary so that the UI can render the complete detail page and any downstream time-tracking actions can reuse the record without refetching.

responseBody.description: The full timelog record.

operations.description:
Update an existing employee timelog entry.

This operation allows a finalized work record to be revised within the currently selected organization context. A timelog represents an employee’s recorded time on a project, with an optional task reference, work description, and billable classification. The updated entry remains tied to the same organizational boundary and must continue to represent the same employee-owned time record after validation and persistence.

The service must verify that the caller is allowed to change the record, that the timelog belongs to the current organization, and that the requested project and optional task are still valid for a time entry. The system must reject any change that would move the record onto an archived or completed project, because preserved historical timelogs remain visible but new edits cannot violate a closed project’s time-entry rules. If the timelog is included in an approved timesheet, the update must be rejected because approved timesheets lock the included timelogs.

If a task is provided, the task must belong to the same project as the timelog and must be compatible with the employee’s work record. The update should preserve the existing ownership and organizational scope while allowing corrections to duration, work description, billable status, project, and task according to business validation rules. After saving, the response should return the refreshed timelog view so clients can display the updated time entry immediately.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target timelog by timelogId within the authenticated user's selected organization scope.

Authorize the request against the timelog owner and/or organization time-management permission according to the platform's permission model. Reject access if the record is not found in the current organization, if the caller is outside the organization boundary, or if the caller is not allowed to edit the record.

Before updating, enforce the following validations:
- The timelog must not be locked by an approved timesheet.
- The target project must belong to the same organization and must not be archived or completed.
- If taskId is provided, the task must belong to the same project as the timelog.
- The request must not change employee ownership; timelog ownership is fixed to the original employee.
- Duration/date/work description/billable fields should be validated according to timelog rules and local business constraints.

Perform the update in a transaction if project/task validation or derived-field recalculation is required. Recompute any persisted derived values such as total duration normalization or day-boundary alignment if the domain model stores them. If the update would conflict with a locked or invalid state, return a domain validation error rather than partially applying changes.

Do not touch timesheet membership records directly in this endpoint. This operation only updates the timelog entity itself; timesheet add/remove behavior is handled by the timesheet draft management endpoints. Return the updated timelog after persistence, including project and optional task references needed for client refresh.

responseBody.description: Updated timelog record.

requestBody.description: Fields used to update the timelog.

operations.description:
Permanently removes a timelog from the currently selected organization.

A timelog is the organization-scoped record of an employee’s recorded work time. It belongs to one employee, is associated with one project, may optionally reference one task, and may later be included in a timesheet. This operation deletes exactly one timelog record identified by its timelog ID and applies only within the active organization context.

Deletion is allowed for the employee who owns the timelog only while that timelog is still eligible for removal. Once the timelog has been included in a submitted timesheet, the request must be rejected so the submitted work history remains stable during review. If the timelog has already been approved through a timesheet, it must also remain protected from removal. Users with timelog management access may delete any employee’s timelogs in the same organization context, but the same submission and approval protections still apply.

This endpoint supports organization-level intervention on time records and should be used together with the list and detail timelog operations when users need to inspect a record before removal. The service must validate organization membership, confirm the current user’s access level, verify that the timelog belongs to the selected organization, and reject deletion when the timelog is locked by a submitted or approved timesheet. On success, the record is permanently removed and no timelog data is returned.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement a timelog deletion command scoped to the authenticated user's selected organization.

Service flow:
1. Resolve the active organization from the authenticated request context.
2. Load the timelog by timelogId with organization scoping to prevent cross-tenant access.
3. If the record does not exist in the active organization, return not found.
4. Determine authorization:
   - allow if the current employee owns the timelog and the record is still deletable,
   - or allow if the current user has timelog management access in the same organization.
5. Enforce deletion eligibility checks before removing the row:
   - reject if the timelog belongs to a submitted timesheet,
   - reject if the timelog belongs to an approved timesheet,
   - reject if business rules indicate the timelog is no longer eligible for deletion.
6. Perform deletion in a transaction so any related cleanup or invariant checks remain consistent.
7. Return success with no response payload.

Business rules and validation:
- Do not allow deletion outside the selected organization.
- Do not allow deletion of a timelog that is already protected by timesheet submission or approval.
- Do not allow a non-owner to delete another employee's timelog unless timelog management access is present.
- Preserve project, task, and timesheet integrity by only deleting the timelog row after eligibility is confirmed.

Implementation notes:
- Query the timelog together with any timesheet-linkage state needed to decide eligibility.
- If the schema uses a join table for timesheet inclusion, check the associated timesheet status before deletion.
- Do not cascade-delete timesheets or other time records.
- Emit an organization activity record only if the service layer already uses activity logging for destructive timelog actions; otherwise do not invent new audit behavior.
- Return standard authorization and validation errors for forbidden and conflict conditions.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of weekly timesheets for the current organization context.

A timesheet represents one employee's time entries for one week, running from Monday through Sunday. This endpoint is designed for browsing weekly timesheet records in a paginated list, with filtering by status and date range so users can narrow the set of timesheets shown on screen.

The response is scoped to the authenticated user's selected organization and respects employee visibility rules. Employees can view their own timesheets, while users with approval authority can also review submitted timesheets that are waiting for approval or rejection. The list reflects the timesheet header record stored in the timesheet table, including week start, week end, status, total hours, submission timestamp, review metadata, and rejection reason.

This operation depends on the organization context already being selected after authentication. The client should not attempt to infer timesheet scope from the URL; instead, the server resolves the active organization and applies employee-level access rules before querying the weekly timesheet records. For review workflows, this endpoint is typically used together with the timesheet detail and review operations that approve or reject a submitted record.

Records returned here are historical workflow records and remain available even when an employee is deactivated or reactivated. The operation must preserve that history and must not remove or hide preserved timesheets solely because an employee's membership status has changed.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a paginated timesheet search over hrm_time_tracking_timesheets using the authenticated member's active organization context.

Query by organization_id from the current request context and constrain visibility by the caller's access level: employees may only see their own timesheets, while approval-capable users may also query submitted timesheets available for review within the organization. Apply optional filters for status and week/date range using week_start and week_end boundaries. Validate that any supplied date range aligns with the Monday-to-Sunday weekly concept.

Use ordering that is stable for paging, preferably week_start descending and then created_at or id as a tiebreaker. Join the employee and reviewedByEmployee relations only as needed for response shaping. Compute or expose total hours from the related timelog inclusion set if the summary schema requires it; do not duplicate timesheet membership data in this query. Return a paginated summary response.

Enforce business rules at the service layer: reject cross-organization access, exclude records outside the selected employee scope, and keep historical timesheets visible for preserved employee records. Do not allow this operation to mutate status or inclusion state; it is strictly read/search only. Surface validation-friendly errors for invalid date ranges, unsupported status values, or unauthorized access.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet summaries.

requestBody.description: Timesheet search filters, pagination, and sorting options.

operations.description:
Create a new weekly timesheet draft for the current employee.

A timesheet represents one employee’s weekly time collection for a Monday-to-Sunday period within the selected organization. This operation creates the timesheet container in draft status and prepares it for later submission, review, approval, or rejection. The created record is bound to the authenticated employee in the active organization context, and the request must not attempt to create a timesheet for another employee.

The weekly boundary must be validated carefully. The requested week must resolve to a single Monday start date and the corresponding Sunday end date, matching the business definition of a timesheet as a weekly collection. The service should reject dates outside the allowed weekly range or requests that would create ambiguous week coverage. If weekly timelogs are attached during creation, they must belong to the same employee, the same organization, and the same week, and they must not already be locked by an approved timesheet.

This endpoint is the first step in the timesheet workflow. After creation, the employee may add or remove eligible timelogs, then submit the timesheet for review. Submitted timesheets are reviewed through separate approval and rejection operations by users with timesheet approval permission. The response includes the timesheet summary fields used throughout that workflow, including total hours and review metadata when available.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implement a timesheet creation service for the authenticated employee in the selected organization.

1. Resolve the current member identity and selected organization from the request context. Do not accept employeeId or organizationId from the body.
2. Validate the requested week. Normalize the provided date to the Monday of that week and compute the corresponding Sunday end date. Reject requests that do not map cleanly to a weekly Monday-Sunday window.
3. Enforce one timesheet container per employee per week in the organization. If the schema or service rules permit only one row per employee/week, check for an existing timesheet before insert and decide whether to return conflict or reuse existing draft according to the implementation policy.
4. Load eligible timelogs for the employee, organization, and week only if the request includes initial inclusion behavior. Exclude timelogs that are already tied to an approved timesheet or otherwise locked. Ensure only the employee’s own timelogs are considered.
5. Insert the timesheet with draft status, week_start_date, week_end_date, and any initialized totals. If included timelogs are stored via join records, create those join rows in the same transaction after the timesheet insert.
6. Compute total hours from included timelogs if the design stores the aggregate on the timesheet row. Recalculate from source timelogs rather than trusting client-provided totals.
7. Return the created timesheet with review metadata fields set to null when not yet submitted/reviewed.
8. Handle errors: forbidden when the user has no employee context in the organization, conflict when a timesheet already exists for the same employee/week, validation failure for invalid week boundaries or illegal timelog inclusion, and not found when referenced timelogs do not belong to the employee or organization.
9. Record any organization activity only if the broader system explicitly logs timesheet creation; otherwise keep this endpoint focused on the timesheet tables and join records.

Use a transaction to ensure the timesheet row and any initial timelog link rows are created atomically.

responseBody.description: The newly created weekly timesheet draft.

requestBody.description: Weekly timesheet creation details for the current employee.

operations.description:
Retrieve the detailed view of a single weekly timesheet.

A timesheet represents one employee's time entries for exactly one week, and that week runs from Monday through Sunday. This operation returns the complete timesheet record for the requested period, including its ownership, weekly coverage, current review status, included timelogs, and review metadata needed by the client to present a full timesheet detail or review screen.

Access to this resource is always evaluated inside the currently selected organization context. An employee can view only their own timesheets. Users with timesheet approval permission can view submitted timesheets for review, and users with broader time visibility permission can view timesheets across employees in the organization. The server must reject requests that do not match the caller's organization scope or visibility rights.

The response is intended to be used together with the timesheet list and timesheet review operations. List endpoints are useful for browsing and filtering weekly records, while this endpoint provides the full single-record view once a specific timesheet has been selected. If the timesheet is submitted, the response should include the metadata required for approval or rejection workflows; if it is still in draft, the response should include the weekly collection details used for editing and submission.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load one timesheet by primary identifier within the active organization context.

Implementation should:
- Validate that the caller is authenticated and has an active organization context.
- Fetch the timesheet by id and ensure it belongs to the selected organization.
- Enforce visibility rules:
  - The employee owner can read their own timesheet.
  - An approver with timesheet approval permission can read submitted timesheets.
  - A user with view-all timelogs/timesheets permission can read any timesheet in the organization.
- Join the related employee record and, when needed for the detail view, the timesheet timelog links and their underlying timelog records.
- Return the weekly range as stored for the timesheet, which must represent Monday through Sunday.
- Include any stored review metadata such as submission state and reviewer information if present in the schema.
- Preserve immutability of read-only historical information; no mutations occur in this endpoint.

Error handling should cover:
- 404 when the timesheet does not exist in the active organization.
- 403 when the caller lacks permission to view the timesheet.
- 400 when the id path parameter is malformed.

The endpoint should not infer data from other weeks or synthesize totals beyond what the service layer can compute from related timelogs and stored values. If totals are stored, return them directly; if they are computed, compute them consistently from the linked timelogs.

responseBody.description: Detailed timesheet information including weekly range, ownership, status, and included timelogs.

operations.description:
Update a single weekly timesheet record for the selected organization.

This operation updates the timesheet header and review metadata for one employee-owned weekly time collection. A timesheet represents one employee's Monday-to-Sunday time collection and stores the workflow state that governs whether the record is still being edited, has been submitted for review, has been approved, or has been rejected. The resource is backed by the `hrm_time_tracking_timesheets` table, which stores the organization boundary, owning employee, reviewer reference, week start and end dates, workflow status, submission timestamp, review timestamp, and rejection reason.

Access to this endpoint is organization-scoped and permission-aware. The employee who owns the timesheet may update their own draft record, while users with timesheet approval permission may update review-related fields when processing submitted timesheets. The organization context in the authenticated session must match the timesheet's `organization_id`, and the record must belong to that organization before any update is applied.

The update must preserve the weekly Monday-to-Sunday structure described by the business model. If the timesheet is moved through the review workflow, the service layer must enforce the rules that submitted timesheets remain available for review, approved timesheets lock the included timelogs, and rejected timesheets return to draft status with a rejection reason. Historical timesheets must remain preserved even when an employee is deactivated or reactivated, so this endpoint must never remove or recreate the record as part of workflow handling.

This endpoint is typically used together with the timesheet list and detail retrieval operations, and with the submission, approval, and rejection workflow actions that manage the record's state. Validation failures should be returned when the requested update conflicts with the current status, violates week boundaries, or attempts to modify fields that are not allowed in the current workflow state.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by id with an organization scope check using organization_id and the authenticated organization context. Reject the request with 404 if the record does not exist in the current organization.

Allow updates only to the fields supported by the timesheet domain model and business rules: week_start, week_end, status, reviewed_by_employee_id, reviewed_at, submitted_at, and rejection_reason as applicable to the current lifecycle state. Do not permit changes to employee_id or organization_id through this endpoint. The service should validate that week_start is a Monday and week_end is the corresponding Sunday for the same weekly range. If the contract allows editing a draft timesheet only, reject attempts to alter workflow metadata outside allowed transitions.

When the request changes status to submitted, enforce the business rule that no other submitted timesheet may already exist for the same employee and week. When changing to approved, require a valid reviewer context with approval permission, set reviewed_by_employee_id and reviewed_at, and ensure included timelogs become locked through the timesheet-timelog relationship. When changing to rejected, require rejection_reason, set reviewed_by_employee_id and reviewed_at, and return the record to draft state if the workflow requires that behavior. Use a transaction so that timesheet header updates and any dependent timelog locking or workflow adjustments remain consistent.

Validate that submitted_at, reviewed_at, and rejection_reason are coherent with the status being written. For example, rejection_reason must be present for rejected state, reviewed_by_employee_id must reference an employee in the same organization, and review timestamps must not precede the submission timestamp. Preserve created_at and updated_at automatically. Return the full updated timesheet entity after persistence.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet record with review metadata and workflow state.

requestBody.description: Editable timesheet fields and workflow-related update values.

operations.description:
Delete a single timesheet that is still eligible for removal.

This operation removes one organization-scoped weekly timesheet record for the authenticated employee in the current organization context. It is intended for draft or otherwise deletable timesheets only, and it must reject requests for timesheets that have already been submitted for review or approved, because those states protect the included time entries and preserve the employee's historical work record.

The timesheet domain represents a weekly time collection for one employee, and the deletion must respect that relationship. The service should verify the target timesheet belongs to the current organization and is accessible to the authenticated member. If the timesheet is linked to submitted or approved review state, the request must fail. If the timesheet is deletable, the service should remove the timesheet record and any join records that associate timelogs to that timesheet, while leaving the underlying timelog records intact.

This endpoint is part of the employee time management workflow and should be used together with timesheet creation, submission, approval, rejection, and list/detail retrieval operations. Historical timesheets for inactive employees remain preserved by business rule, so deletion must not be used to alter past approved history or to affect other employees' records. Permission checks and organization-context checks must be enforced before any database mutation occurs.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement as an organization-scoped delete command against hrm_time_tracking_timesheets.

1. Resolve the authenticated member and active organization context.
2. Load the target timesheet by timesheetId and ensure it belongs to the active organization and is visible to the caller.
3. Enforce deletion eligibility:
   - Reject if the timesheet is submitted, approved, rejected-and-locked, or otherwise non-draft according to the service's timesheet state model.
   - Reject if the record is not owned by the current employee when the caller is limited to self-service deletion.
4. If eligible, execute the deletion in a transaction:
   - Delete associated hrm_time_tracking_timesheet_timelogs join rows for this timesheet.
   - Delete the hrm_time_tracking_timesheets record.
   - Do not delete underlying hrm_time_tracking_timelogs records.
5. Return a standard deleted-resource response.

Edge cases and validation:
- Return 404 when the timesheet does not exist in the active organization scope.
- Return 403 when the caller lacks rights to delete the target employee's timesheet.
- Return 409 when the timesheet is already submitted, approved, or otherwise protected by review state.
- Use a transaction to avoid orphaned join rows.
- Preserve all historical timelog data; only the timesheet association is removed.

No request body is required. The endpoint should remain narrow and resource-specific.

operations.description:
Manage the authenticated employee’s live timer session in the currently selected organization.

A timer session represents the active tracking session used for real-time work recording before it becomes a finalized timelog. This operation is used to start a timer with a project, edit the running timer’s project, task, or description, stop the active timer to convert it into a timelog, or discard the active timer without creating a timelog. The timer session preserves the start timestamp and the running work details while it is active so the system can later compute the final duration correctly.

This endpoint is restricted to the current member in the current organization context. A member can only operate on their own running timer, and one employee can have at most one active timer at a time. If a timer is already active, starting another one must be rejected. If a running timer’s task is changed, the task must belong to the currently selected project. If the project is changed while the timer is running, the existing task must remain valid for the new project or be cleared/replaced so the session stays valid.

When the timer is stopped, the system must convert the live timer session into a finalized timelog using the start timestamp and stop moment to calculate the duration, while preserving the selected project, optional task, and optional description that were used during the running session. When the timer is discarded, no timelog is created and the timer is no longer treated as active. This operation is commonly used together with timelog and timesheet features, because the finalized result may later be included in weekly time review and approval workflows.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement this as an organization-scoped live timer control endpoint for the authenticated member.

Service flow:
1. Resolve the authenticated user’s selected organization context and employee record.
2. Load the employee’s active timer session, if any, using the employee ID and organization ID.
3. Interpret the request body action and perform exactly one of the supported transitions:
   - start: create a new active timer session only if none exists for the employee
   - update: modify the current running session’s project, task, and/or description
   - stop: finalize the active timer into a timelog and mark the timer session inactive
   - discard: end the active timer without creating a timelog
4. Return the latest timer session state after the transition, or the stopped/discarded result as appropriate.

Validation and business rules:
- Reject requests when the caller has no employee membership in the selected organization.
- Reject if another active timer already exists for the employee when attempting to start a new one.
- For project changes, ensure the session remains valid for the new project.
- For task changes, confirm the task belongs to the currently selected project.
- If changing the project makes the current task invalid, the task must be cleared or replaced before saving.
- Do not allow edits once the timer is no longer active.
- Do not allow operations on another employee’s timer.
- Preserve the start timestamp while the timer is active; never rewrite it during edits.

Persistence and transaction handling:
- Use a transaction when stopping a timer so creation of the timelog and deactivation of the timer are atomic.
- Use a transaction when discarding a timer so the session cannot remain active after discard.
- On stop, compute duration from start timestamp to the stop moment and create the timelog with the same organization, employee, project, optional task, and description.
- On update, only modify mutable running fields and any required validity adjustments; do not alter historical state.

Error handling:
- Return a validation error if the request attempts an invalid action or references a task outside the selected project.
- Return a conflict error if a start is requested while an active timer already exists.
- Return not found if there is no active timer to update, stop, or discard.
- Return forbidden if the current organization context or employee ownership does not permit the action.

Implementation note:
- This endpoint is intentionally modeled as PATCH because it is a state transition endpoint with multiple supported mutations rather than a simple read or single-resource update. Keep the contract aligned with the running timer workflow and avoid exposing other employees’ sessions through this route.

responseBody.description: A paginated result containing the current running timer session state after the requested action.

requestBody.description: Timer action and mutable running-session fields.

operations.description:
Start a new live timer session for the currently selected organization context.

This operation creates the running work record used for real-time time tracking while an employee is actively working. The created timer session stores the employee who owns the timer, the selected project, an optional task within that project, the moment the timer started, and an optional description that explains the work being tracked.

A member may only start a timer for the employee record that belongs to the current organization context, and only one active timer session may exist for that employee at a time. The selected task, when provided, must belong to the selected project. If the project does not belong to the current organization, if the task does not belong to the project, or if another active timer already exists, the request must be rejected.

The timer session remains open until it is stopped or discarded by a later timer-session operation. Stopping the session converts the running work record into a timelog, while discarding the session closes it without creating a timelog. The returned timer session data reflects the live state that will be used by those later operations.

This endpoint is intended for authenticated members only and depends on the current organization context being resolved before the request is processed. The organization scope is not passed in the URL because the timer belongs to the employee in the active membership context, not to a free-standing global resource.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Authenticate the member and resolve the selected organization context first. Load the employee record for the current member within that organization. Reject the request if no employee context exists.

Validate the request body. Require a project identifier and ensure the project belongs to the current organization. If a task identifier is provided, verify that the task belongs to the selected project. Reject mismatched project/task combinations.

Before inserting a new timer session, query for an existing active session for the same employee using the unique employee constraint on the timer session table. An active session is one where ended_at is null and discarded_at is null. If a row already exists, reject the request because only one active timer is allowed per employee.

If validation passes, insert a new timer session row with the employee id, project id, optional task id, current timestamp as started_at, optional description, and null ended_at/discarded_at values. Set created_at and updated_at to the current timestamp. Return the newly created session.

Do not create any timelog here. Timelog creation is handled only when a separate stop operation ends the live session. Preserve the start timestamp exactly as written at creation time.

responseBody.description: The newly created live timer session.

requestBody.description: Timer start data including project, optional task, and description.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single live timer session by its identifier.

A timer session represents the active tracking session used for in-progress work. It stores the running work state for one employee, including the selected project, an optional task within that project, the start timestamp, and the editable description that explains what the employee is working on while the timer is still active.

This operation returns the timer session record identified by `timerSessionId` so the client can display the current timer details, including the start time, the selected project, the optional task, and the timer description. The session may also include closing timestamps when the record has already been stopped or discarded, but the primary purpose of this endpoint is to read one session record directly from the timer session data store.

Access is restricted to the authenticated member within the correct organization context. The service must verify that the requested timer session belongs to the current employee and must not expose another employee's running timer. If the timer session is not available to the requester, the request should fail with an authorization or not-found style response according to the application's security policy.

This endpoint is typically used together with the live timer view and timer control operations. The UI may call this detail endpoint after the timer has been started, edited, stopped, or discarded to refresh the session view and keep the visible timer state synchronized with the persisted record.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
