Load the timer session by primary key and join the related employee, project, and optional task relations as needed for authorization and response composition. Validate that the record exists and belongs to the authenticated employee in the current organization context before returning it.

Because this is a detail lookup, no pagination or search logic is required. Do not mutate the record. If the session has been stopped or discarded, return the stored timestamps and description as persisted; do not infer a new state. If the session is inaccessible because it belongs to another employee, return a not-found or forbidden response per the application's security conventions.

The response should map directly from the timer session table columns and preserve nullable fields such as task, description, ended_at, and discarded_at. Use the identifier from the path parameter only; do not accept any request body. Ensure the endpoint remains read-only and organization-scoped.

responseBody.description: Timer session details for the requested running or completed timer.

operations.description:
Update the currently running timer session for the authenticated employee.

This operation lets a member correct the live work record while the timer is still running. The timer session is the ongoing tracking state that stores the selected project, an optional task within that project, the start timestamp, and an editable description. The record remains the active timer session until it is stopped or discarded, so this endpoint is limited to changes that preserve that live-session state.

The request is evaluated against the hrm_time_tracking_timer_sessions record identified by timerSessionId and must belong to the caller’s current organization context through the owning employee relationship. The employee ownership rule is strict: a timer session can only be edited by the employee who owns it, and only while it is still active. The start timestamp must never be changed by this endpoint, and lifecycle timestamps such as endedAt or discardedAt are not writable here because they are controlled by the stop and discard workflows.

If the selected project is changed, the system must revalidate the optional task against the new project. A task may be present only when it belongs to the selected project, and the update must be rejected if the task would become invalid. If the task is provided, it must remain a valid task for the current project after the update. The description may be updated freely while the timer is running and should replace the previous description as the latest work note for the live timer session.

This endpoint is commonly used together with GET /timer-sessions/{timerSessionId} to read the current running timer, and with the stop and discard operations to end the session once the live work has been corrected. If the timer is no longer active, the update must fail because the record is no longer an editable live timer session.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the timer session by timerSessionId and verify it exists, belongs to the current organization, and is owned by the authenticated employee. Reject the request if ended_at or discarded_at is already set, because only a running timer can be edited.

Allow updates only to the mutable live-session fields: selected project, optional task, and description. Never allow changes to started_at, employee ownership, created_at, updated_at, ended_at, discarded_at, or deleted_at from this endpoint. Always preserve the original start timestamp.

When project_id is changed, validate that any provided task_id belongs to the new project. If the task is missing or belongs to another project, reject the request with a validation error rather than silently rewriting the task. If task_id is changed, validate that it belongs to the currently selected project after applying the new value. If the project changes and the existing task no longer belongs to it, the update must either clear the task or be rejected according to service policy; in either case the final persisted session must remain valid.

Before persisting, optionally load the target project and task to confirm they are active and available for use in live tracking. Reject references to projects that are archived or completed if the business layer forbids new live tracking on them. Use a single transactional update so the live session cannot be partially changed.

Return the updated timer session after persistence so the client can refresh the live timer UI. If the employee does not own the timer session, return a forbidden or not found style error consistent with the service's authorization pattern. If the timer is not active, return a conflict or validation error indicating the live session can no longer be edited.

responseBody.description: Updated live timer session.

requestBody.description: Mutable fields for the running timer session.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of activity log entries for the currently selected organization.

Each activity record represents a significant business action that occurred within the organization, including the time of the action, the user who performed it, the action type, the target entity, and supporting details. The log is intended for organizational review and audit visibility, so the returned records must remain anchored to the active organization context and must never include entries from any other organization.

Access to this endpoint is limited to users who are allowed to view organization-level operational history. The response is designed for browsing and filtering historical business events, not for editing or deleting them. Consumers should treat the returned entries as immutable historical facts that help the organization understand what happened and when.

The endpoint supports filtered and paginated retrieval so clients can narrow results by action type, actor, target entity, and date range. The system must apply organization isolation before evaluating any other filters, and any request that attempts to reach outside the current organization must be rejected. For detailed inspection of a single activity entry, a separate detail endpoint should be used if present; this operation is intentionally focused on list browsing.

The underlying hrm_time_tracking_activity_records data model stores append-only entries for significant actions. This API should surface the fields needed for timeline rendering and operational review, while keeping the payload compact enough for fast log browsing. The activity log remains available as historical context for related workflows such as employee changes, contract updates, project actions, task status changes, and other notable organizational events.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement an organization-scoped activity log search on hrm_time_tracking_activity_records.

Resolve the active organization from the authenticated request context first. Reject the request if no organization is selected or if the caller lacks organization-management visibility for activity records. All queries must be constrained to the active organization before any other filtering is applied.

Support paginated filtering by action type, actor user, target entity type, target entity identifier, and date range. Sort newest-first by the activity timestamp by default, with optional stable secondary sorting by primary key if needed for consistent pagination. Because this is a historical log, do not allow mutation operations through this endpoint.

Query the activity records table directly, selecting only the fields needed for summary browsing. If the schema includes a foreign key or actor reference, join or resolve it only for display purposes; do not expose any cross-organization data. Apply validation to ensure any supplied user or target entity filters belong to the current organization context when those fields are organization-scoped.

Return a paginated page object containing summary items with timestamp, actor display reference, action type, target entity metadata, and details summary. Preserve append-only semantics: records are never edited through this endpoint. Handle empty result sets gracefully with an empty page and pagination metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated activity log entries for the active organization.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for organization activity records.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single organization activity record by its identifier.

This operation returns one timestamped business action from the currently selected organization. Each activity record represents a significant operational event in the organization’s history and includes when the event occurred, who performed it, the action type, the affected target entity, and the structured details needed to understand the event in context.

The record is read within the active organization boundary only. A member who belongs to multiple organizations must still access the log through the currently selected organization context, and the API must reject any attempt to read a record that belongs to another organization. This preserves the organization-specific history model described by the activity log requirements and ensures that records are interpreted only inside the organization that owns them.

Access to this endpoint is intended for members with organization management visibility, because the activity log is used as a reviewable history of important business actions such as employee changes, contract updates, project lifecycle changes, task status changes, timesheet decisions, and role assignments. If the requested identifier does not exist in the current organization context, the service should respond as not found rather than exposing whether the record exists elsewhere.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the activity record by primary identifier and the authenticated member's selected organization context.

Implementation steps:
1. Resolve the current organization from the authenticated request context.
2. Query hrm_time_tracking_activity_records by activity_record_id and organization_id together so that cross-organization access is impossible.
3. Join or separately resolve the actor reference if the response schema exposes actor identity details, but only within the same organization scope and without leaking unrelated membership data.
4. Return a single record when found; otherwise return 404.

Validation and access rules:
- Require organization management permission to access this endpoint.
- Reject requests from members who do not have visibility to the organization activity log.
- Never return records from a different organization, even if the same user belongs to both organizations.
- Do not accept any query or body parameters; the path identifier and selected organization context are sufficient.

Data handling:
- Treat the activity record as historical fact data; do not mutate it here.
- Preserve the timestamp, acting user reference, action type, target entity metadata, and detail payload exactly as stored.
- If the schema stores the target entity as structured fields rather than a nested object, map those fields directly in the response model.

Error behavior:
- 404 when no record exists in the current organization for the supplied identifier.
- 403 when the caller lacks organization management access.
- 401 when authentication is missing or invalid.

responseBody.description: The requested organization activity record.

operations.description:
Accept a pending organization invitation using the invitation token embedded in the URL.

This operation completes the invitation fulfillment flow for a pending invitation record that preserves the invited email address and the organization association while the invitation is awaiting action. When the token is valid and the invitation is still pending, the system converts that pending invitation into organizational membership for the invited account and makes the person available inside the target organization without requiring a separate manual onboarding step.

The acceptance flow is tied to the organization that issued the invitation and must honor the invitation rules around pending state, email association, and multiple concurrent invitations for the same email address. If several organizations have pending invitations for the same email, each matching invitation must be processed independently according to its own record. If the token is invalid, expired, already used, or does not correspond to a pending invitation, the request must fail with an appropriate validation or not-found style error.

This endpoint is intended to be used by the invited person as part of the join-organization workflow. It does not modify invitation metadata directly; instead, it executes the business process that consumes the invitation and establishes the organization relationship for the account. The returned result should allow the client to confirm which organization was joined and whether the invitation was successfully fulfilled.
operations.name: accept
operations.specification:
Implement this as a token-scoped invitation fulfillment command.

Steps:
1. Resolve the invitation record by token from the hrm_time_tracking_invitations table.
2. Verify the invitation exists, is still pending, and is eligible for acceptance.
3. Check the invited email stored on the invitation against the currently authenticated member account when an account context exists. If the current request is from a newly created account or a session that has not yet been attached, use the invitation token and invitation email as the source of truth for fulfillment.
4. In a transaction, mark the invitation as accepted/fulfilled according to the actual invitation status model, and create or attach the organization membership/employee linkage required by the domain rules.
5. If there are multiple pending invitations for the same email, process only the invitation addressed by this token; other invitations remain untouched.
6. Prevent double-acceptance by rejecting already-fulfilled tokens.
7. Return the fulfilled invitation outcome, including the organization context and the resulting membership reference if the schema supports it.

Validation and error handling:
- Return 404 when no invitation matches the token.
- Return 409 or validation error when the invitation is no longer pending or has already been consumed.
- Return 422 when the email/account relationship does not match the invitation’s invited email.
- Use a transaction to ensure invitation fulfillment and membership creation are atomic.

Security and authorization:
- Allow the invited user or an authenticated member completing their own invitation flow to call this endpoint.
- Do not require organization-scoped permissions because the invitation token itself authorizes the specific acceptance action.
- Ensure the operation cannot be used to accept a different person’s invitation by comparing the token-bound email association with the current account context where available.

responseBody.description: The fulfilled invitation outcome and resulting organization membership context.

operations.description:
Revoke a pending invitation for an organization and prevent it from being fulfilled later.

This operation is used when an organization no longer wants an invited email address to remain eligible for automatic membership creation. The invitation belongs to the organization that created it, preserves the invited email address, and may coexist with other pending invitations for the same email in other organizations. Revoking one invitation affects only that invitation record and does not interfere with unrelated pending invitations or existing memberships elsewhere.

Access to this action is restricted to members with employee management permission in the current organization context. The authenticated user must be acting inside the organization that owns the invitation, and the invitation must still be in a revocable state. If the invitation has already been resolved into membership because the invited person signed up with the matching email address, the request must be rejected because the invitation can no longer be used for onboarding.

This operation is closely related to invitation listing and invitation creation endpoints. A client typically lists pending invitations, revokes one when needed, and then refreshes the invitation list to reflect the updated status. The returned invitation data allows the UI to show the final state immediately after the action completes.
operations.name: revoke
operations.specification:
Load the invitation by invitationId within the current organization context. Verify the authenticated member has employee management permission for that organization before performing any change.

Check that the invitation exists, belongs to the current organization, and is still pending or otherwise revocable. If the invitation has already been fulfilled, expired, or is otherwise not eligible for revocation according to business rules, return a conflict-style error and do not modify data.

Apply the revocation as a state transition on the invitation record. Preserve the invited email address and organization association for auditability, but mark the invitation as revoked so it cannot be used for future membership fulfillment. Do not touch other invitations that share the same email address. Do not create or delete membership records as part of revocation.

If the persistence model uses a status field, update only that field and any revocation timestamp or reason fields that already exist in the schema; do not assume additional columns. If the model instead uses a dedicated action marker, persist the revocation in the smallest possible write consistent with schema constraints. Return the updated invitation after the transaction commits.

Ensure the operation is idempotent only if the business layer explicitly supports repeated revocation requests. Otherwise, a second revocation attempt on the same invitation should fail with a clear domain error. Emit an activity record only if the application already records invitation lifecycle actions and such a schema exists in the loaded model set.

responseBody.description: The revoked invitation record.

parameters.description: Identifier of the invitation to revoke.
parameters.name: invitationId

operations.description:
Deactivate an employee record within the currently selected organization.

This operation changes the employee's current status from active to deactivated while preserving the underlying employee record and all historical organization data. The employee remains identifiable as part of the organization history, but can no longer log time or submit timesheets in that organization after deactivation.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to users who have employee management permission in the current organization. The server must verify that the specified employee belongs to the selected organization before applying the status transition. If the employee does not belong to the current organization, or if the caller lacks permission to manage employees, the request must be rejected.

The deactivation process should not remove related historical records such as timelogs, timesheets, contracts, or prior role history. Those records remain intact so that reporting, auditing, and recovery workflows can continue to reference the employee as a historical member of the organization. This endpoint is the direct counterpart to the employee reactivation flow, which restores a deactivated employee to active status.
operations.name: deactivate
operations.specification:
Implement a state-transition endpoint that marks one organization-scoped employee as deactivated.

Authorize the caller using the current organization context and require employee management permission. Resolve the employee by employeeId within the current organization only; do not allow cross-organization access. If the employee does not belong to the selected organization, return a not-found or forbidden-style error according to the service error policy.

Perform the status transition in a transaction. Update the employee's current status field to the deactivated value only if the employee is currently active. If the employee is already deactivated, the endpoint should be idempotent and return the current employee representation without changing historical data. Do not delete the employee row and do not cascade-remove contracts, timelogs, timesheets, or other related records.

After the status update, write any required activity/audit record if the application uses the organization activity log for employee lifecycle events. Ensure downstream rules that prevent deactivated employees from logging time or submitting timesheets are enforced by other service-layer checks that read the employee status.

Return the updated employee resource so the client can confirm the new status and continue using the preserved historical membership record.

responseBody.description: The deactivated employee record after the status change.

parameters.description: The employee to deactivate within the current organization.
parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Reactivate a previously deactivated employee in the current organization and restore the employee to active status.

This operation is used by users who have employee management permission to reverse an employee deactivation within the organization that owns the employee record. The employee remains the same organization-specific membership record; reactivation does not create a new employee entry and does not alter preserved historical data such as past timelogs, timesheets, or contracts.

When the employee is restored to active status, the employee can again log time and submit timesheets according to the organization’s rules and the employee’s assigned role. The server must verify that the target employee belongs to the currently selected organization context before applying the status change. If the employee is already active, does not exist, or belongs to a different organization, the request must be rejected.

This endpoint is part of the employee management lifecycle and is typically used together with employee detail retrieval and employee list management screens. It supports the business rule that deactivated employees can be reactivated in the same organization without losing their historical records.
operations.name: reactivate
operations.specification:
Load the target employee by employeeId within the authenticated user's selected organization context.
Verify that the caller has employee management permission before any modification.
Confirm that the employee exists and belongs to the current organization; otherwise return a not-found or forbidden-style error as appropriate for the security model.

Check the employee's current status. If the employee is already active, reject the request as an invalid state transition. If the employee is deactivated, update the employee status to active in a single transactional write.

Do not create a new employee record and do not modify historical timelogs, timesheets, contracts, or related historical records. Preserve all existing employee attributes such as department, role assignment, and employment metadata unless the schema or business rules explicitly require status-only changes.

If the application records significant business actions, append an activity record describing that the employee was reactivated by the acting user in the organization context.
Return the updated employee entity after persistence so the client can refresh its view.
Handle concurrency safely so that repeated reactivation requests do not corrupt state; treat the operation as idempotent only if the implementation chooses to return the active employee for an already-active record, otherwise reject the second request consistently.

responseBody.description: The employee record after reactivation.

parameters.description: Employee record to reactivate within the current organization.
parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Update an employee membership record within the active organization.

This endpoint allows an authorized organization member with employee management access to edit the current organization-scoped employee record that links a user account to the tenant. The employee record is the core staffing entity for the organization, and it holds the current department placement, position title, employment type, and employment status for that membership.

The update is always evaluated within the currently selected organization context. The system must confirm that the target employee belongs to that same organization before applying any changes. Requests that target an employee from another organization must be rejected, even if the caller has a valid account in both organizations.

This operation does not modify the employee's global user account or shared profile. It only updates the organization-specific membership record. Role reassignment is intentionally not included here because each employee can hold exactly one role in an organization, and role changes are managed through a separate role-assignment workflow to preserve the current role history and avoid ambiguous updates.

Validation must ensure that any referenced department exists in the active organization, that employment type and status values are valid for the organization’s workforce rules, and that empty or null department values are handled as an explicit unassignment. The response returns the updated employee record so that employee lists, department views, and staffing screens can refresh immediately after a successful change.
operations.name: patchByEmployeeid
operations.specification:
Load the employee by id and constrain the query to the active organization context. If no employee is found for that organization, return a not-found or access-denied error consistent with the platform's security policy.

Validate the request body fields before persistence. Allow partial updates only for mutable columns such as department_id, position_title, employment_type, and status. Do not allow changes to id, organization_id, user_account_id, role_id, created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at from this endpoint.

If department_id is provided, verify that the department belongs to the same organization. If the department does not belong to the active tenant, reject the request. If department_id is null, clear the employee's department assignment.

Validate employment_type and status against the application's allowed workforce values. If the service uses an enum or reference list for these fields, enforce it at the service layer and return a validation error for unsupported values.

Persist the update in a single transaction. Update the employee row and refresh updated_at. If additional business logging is required by the system, emit an activity record after the employee update succeeds, but do not let audit logging change the update result.

Do not cascade role or contract changes from this endpoint. Do not alter user account linkage. Do not touch organization ownership, membership, or profile data. This endpoint is strictly for organization-scoped employee profile edits.

responseBody.description: Updated employee membership record.

parameters.description: Target employee ID within the active organization.
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the employee membership record.

operations.description:
Update a custom role within the currently selected organization.

This endpoint modifies the organization-scoped role definition stored in the role set for the active organization. The role name and permission bundle can be changed only when the target role is a custom role created within that same organization. Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee remain fixed organization-wide role options and cannot be edited through this operation.

The update is evaluated within the current organization context. The system must first confirm that the target role belongs to the selected organization, then verify that the caller is allowed to manage organization roles. Any permission changes must use only the predefined business capabilities already supported by the platform. When the role’s permission set changes, the new capabilities apply immediately to every employee assigned to that role in the organization because each employee has exactly one role in that organization at a time.

This operation should return the updated role with its permissions so clients can refresh role-management interfaces after saving changes. Validation failures should be returned when the role is built-in, when the role does not belong to the active organization, or when the requested permission set contains unsupported capabilities.
operations.name: patchByRoleid
operations.specification:
Load the target role by roleId and confirm it belongs to the current organization context derived from authentication/session state. Reject the request with 404 if the role does not exist in the organization boundary.

Before applying changes, determine whether the role is built-in. If it is Owner, Manager, or Employee, reject the update with a business-rule validation error because built-in roles are fixed and not editable. Only custom roles may proceed.

Accept partial role updates focused on role name and permission membership. Apply a uniqueness check for the role name within the same organization if the role schema enforces or business rules require unique names. If permissions are submitted, validate every permission code against the canonical permission catalog and reject any unknown or deprecated capability. Ensure the resulting permission set contains no duplicates.

Persist the update in a transaction that updates the role record and replaces the role-permission associations atomically, so the role cannot be saved with a partially updated permission bundle. If the platform tracks role permission rows separately, delete existing associations for the role and insert the new set in the same transaction.

Do not modify employee records directly here. Employee access changes are a downstream consequence of the role definition update and will take effect when authorization checks read the updated role-permission mapping.

Return the updated role detail including the resolved permission list. Emit an activity record if the system logs organization governance changes. Handle concurrency conflicts if the role was changed between read and write, and surface a clear validation error when the role has become protected or reassigned in a way that violates current rules.

responseBody.description: Updated role details with the effective permission set.

parameters.description: Target role identifier within the current organization.
parameters.name: roleId

requestBody.description: Role name and permission updates for a custom organization role.

operations.description:
Retrieve the role assignment history for a single employee within the current organization.

This endpoint returns the chronological timeline of role assignment records stored in the employee role history table. Each record represents one effective assignment period, including when the role became active and when it ended, so organization managers and other permitted viewers can review how the employee’s organizational role changed over time.

The data is organization-scoped and must be resolved against the currently selected organization context before any rows are returned. The employee identifier in the path must belong to that organization, and the service must reject requests that try to access an employee from another tenant boundary. The response is derived from the employee role history table, which preserves historical role changes separately from the employee’s current role field, ensuring that current state and historical assignment periods remain consistent.

Because the endpoint is read-only, it does not alter employee membership, role membership, or any historical assignment row. The operation should return the assignment timeline in reverse chronological order so the most recent effective assignment is easy to inspect first. The response should include the role reference and assignment period fields needed for display and audit review, while avoiding unrelated employee profile data.

Access to this endpoint should be restricted to authenticated members who are allowed to view employee data in the selected organization. Organization owners and managers should have access by default, and additional employee-self access may be permitted only if organization employee visibility rules allow it. Requests that lack permission, reference an employee outside the current organization, or target a missing employee record should fail with the appropriate authorization or not-found error.
operations.name: history
operations.specification:
Resolve the current organization context from the authenticated member before querying any data.

Validate that the path employeeId belongs to the current organization by loading the employee row from hrm_time_tracking_employees using the composite organization scope and the employee primary key. Reject the request if the employee is missing or belongs to a different organization.

Query hrm_time_tracking_employee_roles for all rows matching hrm_time_tracking_employee_id = employeeId, excluding deleted rows when the business layer treats deleted assignment records as inactive history. Order the results by effective_from descending, and optionally by created_at descending as a stable secondary sort.

Join or hydrate the linked hrm_time_tracking_roles rows so the response includes role identity and presentation fields needed by the UI. Do not include unrelated employee or organization records beyond what is necessary to describe the history row.

This endpoint is read-only and must not mutate any state. No transaction is required beyond the normal read path unless the service layer uses a transaction for consistent read isolation.

Enforce authorization before query execution. Organization owners, managers, or users with employee-view permissions should be allowed; if employee-self access is supported by the policy, allow only when employeeId matches the authenticated member’s employee record in the same organization.

Return a history collection DTO that exposes the assignment period and role details. Preserve null effective_to values to indicate the currently active assignment period.

responseBody.description: Role assignment history records for the employee.

parameters.description: Target employee's ID within the current organization.
parameters.name: employeeId

prerequisites.description: An employee record must exist in the current organization before its role assignment history can be retrieved. This prerequisite creates the employee resource referenced by employeeId and prevents the history lookup from targeting a missing or cross-tenant employee.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full contract history for a single employee within the currently selected organization.

This endpoint returns both the employee's current contract and any historical contracts that belong to the same employee record. It is designed for contract viewing workflows where the consumer needs to understand the employee's employment terms over time, including the active agreement and the preserved past agreements that remain part of the employee's history.

Access is limited to the employee themselves and users who have employee viewing access in the current organization context. The system must confirm that the employee belongs to the selected organization before returning data, and it must not expose contracts from another organization even if the identifier exists elsewhere in the platform.

The response reflects the contract history model used by the underlying employee contract records, which are stored as immutable historical entries once they are no longer active. The current contract should be clearly identifiable in the returned collection, and historical contracts should remain visible so consumers can display the complete employment record. This operation is commonly used together with employee detail retrieval when showing an employee profile, current employment terms, and past contract changes in one view.
operations.name: getByEmployeeid
operations.specification:
Implement a read-only service method that loads all employee contract records for the given employee within the current organization context.

1. Validate that the authenticated member is operating within a selected organization.
2. Resolve the target employee by `employeeId` and ensure the employee belongs to the current organization.
3. Authorize access if the caller is either the employee's own identity or a user with employee viewing access; otherwise return forbidden.
4. Query `hrm_time_tracking_employee_contracts` filtered by employee identifier and organization scope. Preserve all historical rows because contract history is required.
5. Sort results so the active contract appears first, followed by older contracts in descending effective-date order (or equivalent historical ordering supported by the schema).
6. Do not allow any update, creation, or mutation in this operation; it is strictly a retrieval endpoint.
7. If the employee does not exist in the current organization, return not found.
8. If the employee exists but has no contracts, return an empty list rather than an error.

Edge cases:
- A contract marked as current/active must still be returned alongside past contracts.
- Historical contracts must remain visible even when no longer active.
- Cross-organization employee IDs must be rejected before query execution.

Use a collection response type so the UI can render contract history and current contract together without requiring a second API call.

responseBody.description: Employee contract history including the current contract and historical contracts.

parameters.description: Target employee ID within the current organization.
parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Retrieve the permission set assigned to a specific organization role.

This operation returns the capabilities granted to the role identified by the path parameter within the caller’s currently selected organization context. It is intended for role administration screens and authorization inspection flows where organization owners or other authorized users need to see exactly which business capabilities are bundled into a role capability set.

The data is read from the organization-scoped role record and its permission junction records. The role itself belongs to one organization, and each permission grant row links one role to one permission, allowing the system to evaluate access entitlements without duplicating the underlying permission catalog. The response reflects the normalized permission assignments for that role rather than the full role object.

Access to this endpoint must be restricted by organization context and role-management authorization. The roleId must resolve to a role owned by the active organization, otherwise the request must be rejected as not found or forbidden depending on the authorization model. This endpoint does not change any data, does not create or remove permission grants, and should be used together with role detail and role update operations when an organization owner is reviewing or editing a role’s capability set.
operations.name: getByRoleid
operations.specification:
Load the role by roleId and verify that it belongs to the caller’s selected organization context before reading any permission grants.
Join hrm_time_tracking_role_permissions against the role and the permission catalog used by the authorization layer, then return the set of permissions associated with that role in a stable order suitable for client rendering. The query should be read-only and should not include deleted role-permission rows if the domain treats deleted_at as inactive in this context.

Enforce that the authenticated member has the authority to inspect role permissions for the active organization. For organization owners, return the full permission set. For other viewers, only allow access if their assigned permission set explicitly grants role or organization permission visibility. If the role does not exist in the active organization, return a not-found response to avoid leaking cross-tenant data.

Do not paginate unless the implementation layer requires a uniform collection wrapper. The permission list for one role should generally be small, so the response can be returned as a direct collection summary or detail-style payload. If the permission catalog contains metadata such as codes or labels, map them into the response schema for display purposes, but do not expose internal join-table identifiers unless the schema explicitly requires them.

responseBody.description: Permission set assigned to the role.

parameters.description: Target role ID within the active organization.
parameters.name: roleId

operations.description:
Retrieve an overview of a single department within the currently selected organization.

This endpoint returns a compact department view suitable for a department detail or overview page. A department belongs to exactly one organization, may optionally have one parent department to form a one-level hierarchy, and may be used to organize employees inside that organization. The overview should reflect the department’s current organizational placement and present the department information in a way that helps members understand where the department sits in the organization structure.

Access to this endpoint must be evaluated in the context of the authenticated member’s selected organization. A department from another organization must not be visible through this route, and the request must be rejected if the department does not belong to the current organization. The organization-level rules also require that department browsing remain scoped to the active tenant boundary, so the implementation must verify the department ownership before returning any data.

If the department overview includes relationship-derived information such as parent department context or employee association counts, those values must be computed only from records within the same organization. The endpoint must not alter any data, and it must not expose employees from other organizations. Any department that exists in the organization but has no employees assigned must still be readable through this operation as long as it remains part of the organization structure.
operations.name: overview
operations.specification:
Implement this as a read-only department detail-summary endpoint.

Load the department by id and verify that it belongs to the authenticated user’s currently selected organization before returning a response. If the organization context does not match, return a not-found or forbidden-style error consistent with the platform’s tenancy rules. The query should include the department record and, if needed, its parent department reference so the client can render hierarchy context.

If the product requires derived overview data, compute it from organization-scoped records only. For example, any employee count must be filtered by the same organization and by the target department id. Do not attempt to infer data from deleted or out-of-scope departments. The operation must be safe for empty departments and must not require a request body.

Use a single database read path where possible. Because this endpoint is only for viewing, no transaction is needed unless the implementation must coordinate multiple reads for a consistent snapshot. Keep the response shape stable and minimal so it can support a department overview page without exposing unrelated organization or employee data.

responseBody.description: Department overview information.

operations.description:
Retrieve the organization dashboard for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint returns a high-level operational snapshot for the active organization context. The dashboard is intended for users who have report viewing access and need to understand the current state of work at a glance. It summarizes key organizational activity such as active employees, weekly time volume, pending timesheets, high-utilization projects, and top time contributors so that the user can monitor operational health before moving into detailed reports.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to the selected organization. A user who belongs to multiple organizations must only see the dashboard for the organization currently in context, and requests that do not match the active organization must be rejected. If the user does not have the report viewing permission, the system must deny access to the dashboard entirely.

The data returned here is an aggregated view built from organization-scoped operational records. It should combine information from employees, timelogs, timesheets, projects, and activity-related records without exposing records from other organizations. This endpoint is commonly used together with the time report, project budget report, weekly summary report, and activity log to support end-to-end oversight workflows.

The response should be optimized for UI rendering rather than entity editing. It should provide summary metrics and ranked lists that can be displayed on a dashboard page without additional transformation. Because the endpoint is read-only and already scoped by the active organization context, no request body is required.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Implement a read-only dashboard aggregation endpoint for the active organization context.

Authorize the caller using the report viewing permission before any data retrieval. Resolve the currently selected organization from the authenticated member context, then reject the request if the user is not authorized for that organization or if no organization is selected.

Build the dashboard response from organization-scoped aggregates only. Typical source data includes employees, timelogs, timesheets, projects, and any other operational metrics needed for the dashboard cards and rankings. Ensure every query is filtered by organization ID and never joins across tenant boundaries.

Return a single dashboard DTO containing the current operational snapshot. The service should compute summary counts and top lists in a small number of queries, preferably with grouped aggregate queries and limited ranked result sets. Favor efficient read models over loading full entity collections.

Do not accept a request body or search criteria on this endpoint. Any advanced reporting dimensions, such as detailed date range filtering or project-specific analysis, belong in dedicated report endpoints rather than the dashboard overview.

Handle authorization failures with a forbidden response and return a not-found or access-denied style response when the organization context is invalid or unavailable, according to the application's existing error conventions. Ensure the response reflects the active organization only.

responseBody.description: Organization dashboard snapshot for the active organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve the list of projects assigned to the currently authenticated employee in the selected organization context.

This endpoint returns only the projects connected to the employee through project membership records, so the result reflects the employee’s current participation in the organization. It is intended for employee-facing project browsing, allowing a member to quickly see where they contribute without exposing unrelated projects or all organization projects.

Access to this endpoint requires an authenticated member session and a valid selected organization context. The service must resolve the current employee within that organization and then query the project membership relationship to build the result set. Projects that are not linked to the employee through a membership record must not appear in the response, even if the employee has access to other features in the organization.

The response is paginated and uses project summary data suitable for list views. The implementation should preserve the independence of memberships across projects, so changes in one project membership do not affect visibility of other assigned projects. This endpoint is commonly used together with project detail retrieval and task list endpoints, where the assigned project list becomes the entry point for narrowing down work items.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated member and active organization context first. Determine the employee record for the current user in that organization; if no employee exists in the selected organization, return an authorization or context error consistent with the platform’s access model.

Query hrm_time_tracking_project_memberships filtered by the employee identifier from the current organization context. Join to hrm_time_tracking_projects to fetch the project data needed for summary display. Exclude membership records that do not belong to the resolved employee or current organization. If the project schema includes status, archived/completed flags, dates, and visual metadata, include them in the summary projection.

Use stable pagination over the employee’s assigned projects. If the API layer supports search or sorting conventions for project lists, apply the same project-list sorting rules here so the assigned-project view remains consistent with general project browsing. No request body is needed because the endpoint always derives scope from authentication and organization context.

Return only project summaries, not full project aggregates. Do not include membership internals in the response unless the summary schema explicitly requires a membership role field. If membership role is exposed, source it from the current employee-project membership row.

Handle the empty-state case by returning a valid empty page rather than an error when the employee has no assigned projects. Do not widen the query to all organization projects under any circumstance.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of projects assigned to the current employee.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for assigned projects.

operations.description:
Retrieve the employees assigned to a project together with their project membership details.

This endpoint returns the roster of project members for the specified project in the currently selected organization context. It is backed by the project membership join table, which stores the relationship between one project and one employee, and includes the project-lead flag that indicates whether a member has elevated project authority.

The response is intended for project member browsing screens, project administration pages, and task-assignment workflows. It should include the membership record, the linked employee summary, and the organization-scoped account information needed to display a readable member list. The project itself belongs to one organization, so the lookup must always be constrained by both the project identifier in the path and the caller’s organization context.

Access is limited to users who can view the project in the current organization. Users with project view permission can browse assigned project members, while users with project management permission may use related write endpoints to assign or remove members. This operation does not modify membership records and must not expose members from any other project or organization.

The implementation should respect the uniqueness rules of the membership table, which guarantees that one employee can appear only once per project. Deleted or inactive membership records must not be returned if the application layer treats them as removed. The service should order results consistently so UI consumers can render stable member lists and support pagination without duplication.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the target project by projectId in the current organization context, then query project membership records for that project. Join the employee record for each membership, and include the linked user account identity fields needed for display, such as the account email or profile-derived display name if the broader response schema supports it.

Enforce tenant isolation by verifying that the project belongs to the authenticated user's selected organization before loading memberships. Reject the request if the project does not exist in the current organization or if the caller lacks permission to view projects in that organization.

Return memberships in a deterministic order, preferably by creation time and then employee identity, so paging remains stable. Do not return duplicate employee rows; rely on the unique project-employee membership constraint. Exclude any membership rows treated as removed by the application layer. If the project is archived or completed, the members list is still readable unless higher-level permission rules state otherwise.

Because this is a list endpoint, support pagination through the IRequest DTO with page, pageSize, search, and sort fields. Search should apply to employee-facing fields such as name, email, position title, or role label when available from the joined employee/account data. The response should be a page object containing summary items for each project member, including whether the member is a project lead.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project members for the specified project.

parameters.description: Target project ID within the current organization.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for project member browsing.

operations.description:
Update the workflow status of a task that belongs to a specific project.

This operation changes the current task status stored in the task record and records the transition as an immutable history entry. The task remains a project-scoped work item, and the update must be performed only within the project identified by the path parameter so that task movement across projects is never implied or allowed.

The task lifecycle is limited to the supported states of open, in-progress, completed, and closed. When the status changes, the service must persist the new current status on the task and write a corresponding row into the task history store with the previous status, the new status, the acting member, and the transition timestamp. This ensures the system preserves a complete audit trail of how work progressed through the project.

Access is restricted to users who are allowed to manage tasks in the project. A project lead may update tasks in the project where they hold that role, and a user with broader project management permission may update tasks according to their organization access rules. The endpoint must reject requests if the task does not belong to the specified project, if the new status is not one of the supported lifecycle values, or if the requester lacks task management authority for the project.

This operation is typically used alongside task retrieval and task history viewing. Clients may first call the task detail endpoint to inspect the current state, then submit a status transition here, and finally fetch the task history to display the progression trail. The update and history insert must succeed atomically so that the task state and its audit record remain consistent.
operations.name: updateStatus
operations.specification:
Implement this as a project-scoped task status transition endpoint.

Service flow:
1. Resolve the authenticated member and current organization context.
2. Load the project by projectId within the current organization boundary.
3. Load the task by taskId and verify it belongs to the specified project.
4. Verify the requester is authorized to manage the task: either a project lead for the project or a user with project management permission.
5. Validate the requested target status against the allowed task lifecycle values: open, in-progress, completed, closed.
6. Validate the transition against business rules if transition restrictions are enforced by the domain layer.
7. Execute a single transaction that:
   - updates hrm_time_tracking_tasks.status and updated_at;
   - inserts a new row into hrm_time_tracking_task_histories with hrm_time_tracking_task_id, hrm_time_tracking_member_id, from_status, to_status, and changed_at.
8. Return the updated task entity after the transaction commits.

Validation and edge cases:
- Reject if the task is not found in the specified project.
- Reject if the project is not accessible in the current organization.
- Reject if the requester lacks project-lead or project-management authority.
- Reject if the target status is missing or not one of the allowed values.
- Reject if the transition is disallowed by workflow policy.
- Preserve history integrity even when the same status is requested; if idempotent handling is preferred, return the current task without writing a duplicate history entry only when explicitly supported by the domain rules.

Database considerations:
- Use the task table as the authoritative current-state source.
- Use the task history table as the append-only audit record.
- Never move the task to another project in this operation.
- Keep the update and history insert in one transaction to avoid drift between current state and audit trail.

Error handling:
- 400 for invalid status or invalid transition.
- 403 for insufficient permissions.
- 404 when project or task is not found within scope.
- 409 if concurrent updates create a stale status conflict and optimistic locking is implemented.

responseBody.description: Updated task after the status transition has been applied.

parameters.description: Target task identifier within the project.
parameters.name: taskId

requestBody.description: New status to apply to the task.

operations.description:
Retrieve the status change history for a specific task within a project.

This operation returns the immutable audit trail stored in the task history records for the selected task. Each history item captures the task identifier, the member who performed the change, the previous status, the new status, and the timestamp of the transition. The task history table is append-only in practice and exists to preserve the progression of work over time, so this endpoint is intended for timeline display, activity review, and operational traceability.

Access to this endpoint follows the same project-scoped visibility rules as task access itself. Because tasks belong to projects and employees can only view tasks in projects they are assigned to, the caller must already have permission to view the parent project and the selected task. Project leads and users with broader project management permission can review task progress in the projects they can access, while other employees only see history for tasks in their assigned projects.

The operation depends on the parent task being located inside the parent project specified by the path. The implementation must verify that the task belongs to the project before loading any history records. If the task does not exist under that project, the endpoint should return a not-found response rather than exposing cross-project data. The result should be sorted chronologically by the change timestamp so clients can present the task progression in order.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a read-only query that first validates the parent project and task relationship, then loads task history rows for the resolved task ID.

Service flow:
1. Resolve the current organization context from authentication middleware.
2. Verify the caller can access the project according to project visibility rules.
3. Query hrm_time_tracking_tasks by id and hrm_time_tracking_project_id to ensure the task belongs to the specified project and is visible in the current organization.
4. Query hrm_time_tracking_task_histories by hrm_time_tracking_task_id.
5. Join or hydrate the member reference so the response can include who changed the status.
6. Sort by changed_at ascending for timeline presentation, unless the application layer uses a different standard list ordering; chronological order is preferred for history display.

Validation and error handling:
- Return 404 if the project or task cannot be resolved in the current organization context.
- Return 403 if the caller lacks permission to view the project or tasks in that project.
- Return an empty list when the task exists but has no history records.
- Do not accept any request body because the endpoint is a direct collection read.

Data considerations:
- Do not modify task status or history data.
- Do not expose history for tasks in other projects.
- The task history table is immutable audit data, so the endpoint must never attempt updates or deletes.
- If needed for implementation simplicity, preload the associated member and map it into a summary DTO suitable for audit UI rendering.

responseBody.description: A chronological paginated list of task status history entries for the selected task.

parameters.description: Target task ID within the project.
parameters.name: taskId

requestBody.description: Task history list context is fully defined by the path and requires no additional payload.

operations.description:
Retrieve the signed-in employee's own timelogs for the currently selected organization.

This operation returns a paginated list of finalized time entries that belong to the current employee account within the active organization context. Each timelog represents a work record tied to one project, may optionally reference one task in that project, and stores the work date, duration, description, and billable flag used for personal review and weekly reporting.

The response is limited to records whose ownership matches the authenticated employee. Users who have broader visibility permissions may view other employees' timelogs through separate organization-scoped endpoints, but this endpoint always remains self-only and is intended for an employee's personal time browsing flow. The query supports filtering by date range, project, task, and billable status so employees can review work entries at a finer level than project alone.

Use this endpoint together with draft timesheet management when assembling weekly submissions: an employee can review their own timelogs here, then add eligible entries to a draft timesheet before submission. Timelogs that are already locked by an approved timesheet must still appear as historical records, but any edit workflow for those entries must be rejected by the service layer.

The organization context is required implicitly through authentication and selection state. The server must enforce that only the current employee's records are returned, and it must apply tenant isolation using the organization_id and employee_id relationships defined in the timelog table and employee membership table.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a personal timelog listing query for the authenticated member in the selected organization.

Load the current employee membership from the authentication context and selected organization context first. Use employee_id plus organization_id as the hard scope for every query so no other employee's records can be returned.

Query hrm_time_tracking_timelogs with joins to hrm_time_tracking_projects, hrm_time_tracking_tasks, and hrm_time_tracking_employees as needed for filtering and response shaping. Apply optional filters from the request body for work date range, project, task, and billable flag. Task filtering must only match timelogs whose task_id equals the requested task and whose task belongs to the same project, preserving data integrity.

Return paginated results ordered by work_date descending and then created_at descending for stable browsing. Include summary data only: ids, work date, duration, description, billable state, and minimal related project/task/employee display fields needed by the client. Do not expose other employees' timelogs from this endpoint even if broader permissions exist.

Reject requests when the selected organization context is missing, when the authenticated member has no employee membership in that organization, or when filter values are invalid. Enforce that task/project combinations remain consistent, and surface a validation error if the requested task does not belong to the requested project filter. Keep the endpoint read-only and do not allow any write-side mutation.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of the current employee's timelog summaries.

requestBody.description: Personal timelog filters and pagination options.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated organization-wide list of timelogs for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint is designed for users who need broad visibility into employee time entries across the organization. It exposes the finalized timelog records stored in the time tracking subsystem, including the employee who created the entry, the project it belongs to, the optional task association, the work date, duration, billable flag, and descriptive notes. The operation is especially useful for managers, approvers, and users granted organization-wide time visibility.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to members who have permission to view all timelogs in the current organization context. Users without that permission must continue using their own personal timelog views. The API must enforce organization isolation so that only timelogs belonging to the selected organization are returned, and no cross-tenant data is ever exposed.

The request supports structured filtering for operational review, including date range, project, task, employee, and billable criteria, along with pagination and sorting. The response returns a paginated collection of timelog summaries suitable for list screens, dashboards, and approval workflows. Related data such as employee and project labels should be joined in the service layer so that the list can be consumed without additional follow-up requests for basic browsing.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a read-only organization-scoped timelog listing endpoint.

Load the currently selected organization from the authenticated member context, then verify that the caller has organization-wide timelog visibility, such as the time:view_all capability. If the caller lacks this permission, reject the request with a forbidden response rather than falling back to self-only access, because this endpoint is explicitly for organization view.

Build a query against hrm_time_tracking_timelogs constrained by organization_id from the selected organization. Apply optional filters from the request body: work date range, project_id, task_id, employee_id, billable flag, and free-text description search if supported by the shared list DTO pattern. Join hrm_time_tracking_employees to expose employee display data, hrm_time_tracking_projects for project labels, and hrm_time_tracking_tasks when task context is needed. Only include timelogs with the current organization_id; never infer scope from employee/project relationships alone.

Use pagination and deterministic sorting. Prefer descending work date and created_at as the default order so recent activity appears first. If the request includes custom sorting, validate the sort field against allowed columns only. Return a paginated summary DTO rather than full entity detail to keep list payloads compact.

Do not mutate any records. This endpoint must never create timesheets, alter lock state, or change deletion status. Timelogs that belong to approved timesheets remain visible as records but should respect whatever business rules govern editability elsewhere; this endpoint simply reads data. If no rows match the filters, return an empty page result rather than an error.

The response schema should be the standard page container for timelog summaries, and the request schema should be the organization-view list request DTO that carries filters, pagination, and sorting. Ensure the implementation is aligned with the timelog visibility rules and the organization data boundary enforced throughout the time tracking module.

responseBody.description: Paginated organization-wide timelog summaries.

requestBody.description: Organization-wide timelog filters, pagination, and sorting options.

operations.description:
Create a new draft timesheet for the authenticated employee for a selected Monday-to-Sunday week.

This operation starts the weekly time collection workflow for the current employee in the selected organization context. When the draft is created, the system automatically includes that employee’s timelogs that fall within the same week, allowing the employee to review the collected entries before submission. The draft belongs only to the current employee and must not be used to create or inspect another employee’s timesheet.

The returned timesheet represents the draft state of the weekly collection, together with the timelogs that were included at creation time. The employee can then add or remove timelogs through the dedicated draft-management endpoints before submitting the sheet for approval. This endpoint is part of the employee-facing timesheet flow and should be used together with the submission, approval, and rejection operations.

Access is restricted to authenticated members in their own employee context. The server must enforce organization isolation, ensure the selected week is valid, and only attach timelogs owned by the same employee. If the target week already has a submitted or approved timesheet for that employee, the request must be rejected according to the weekly uniqueness rules.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Implement this as an employee-scoped create operation on the timesheet service.

1. Resolve the authenticated member, selected organization context, and the employee record for that context.
2. Validate that the request specifies a Monday-to-Sunday week boundary or a date that can be normalized to that week.
3. Check whether a timesheet already exists for the same employee and week in submitted or approved status; if so, reject the request.
4. Create a new draft timesheet row with the current employee and organization identifiers and the normalized week start/end.
5. Query finalized timelogs for the same employee whose work date falls within that week, and create the join rows in timesheet_timelogs so the draft includes them immediately.
6. Return the created draft timesheet with its included timelogs, any week metadata, and computed totals if the timesheet schema supports them.

Use a transaction to ensure the timesheet row and join rows are created atomically. Validate that every included timelog belongs to the same employee and organization, and reject any attempt to include foreign timelogs. Do not accept employee identifiers in the request body because the authenticated context determines ownership. Preserve draft editability after creation so later endpoints can add or remove timelogs before submission.

responseBody.description: The created draft timesheet with its included weekly timelogs.

requestBody.description: Selected week information for the draft timesheet.

operations.description:
Update the timelog membership of a draft timesheet.

This operation lets an employee revise the weekly collection of time entries before submission by adding timelogs to the draft or removing timelogs that should no longer be included. It operates on the weekly timesheet header defined by the organization, employee, week range, and review metadata, while the actual membership of time entries is stored in the separate timesheet-timelog junction table.

The timesheet must belong to the currently selected organization context and must be in draft status. Draft timesheets remain editable, while submitted, approved, or rejected records follow the timesheet workflow rules and cannot be freely modified in the same way. When a timesheet is approved, the included timelogs are locked by the approval workflow, so this endpoint must reject changes that would violate that lock. When a draft is created for a week, the existing weekly timelogs for the same Monday-to-Sunday period may be present and can then be refined through this endpoint before submission.

The operation is intended for the owning employee to manage their own weekly timesheet contents. Organization-wide time visibility or time-management permissions may allow broader access where the application policy permits it, but the business default is self-service editing of the current employee's draft timesheet. The implementation must ensure every included timelog belongs to the same employee as the timesheet and must not allow cross-employee inclusion.

All additions and removals must be validated against the underlying time entry and timesheet rules. A timelog can be linked to at most one timesheet at a time, so attempting to add a timelog that is already attached to a different timesheet must be rejected. Removing a timelog should delete or deactivate the join record only; it must not alter the underlying timelog facts such as work date, duration, project, task, billable flag, or descriptions. The response returns the updated timesheet with its membership information so the client can re-render the draft weekly editor immediately after the change.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by id within the current organization scope and verify that it belongs to the authenticated employee unless elevated time management permission is present. Confirm the timesheet exists, is not deleted, and is in draft status before allowing any membership changes.

Accept a request body that expresses add/remove membership changes for timelogs. For each timelog to add, fetch the timelog record by id and validate: same organization, same employee as the timesheet owner, within the Monday-to-Sunday week covered by the timesheet, not already linked to another timesheet, and not blocked by approval locks or other workflow restrictions. If the timelog already belongs to this timesheet, ignore the duplicate or return a validation error depending on the platform's consistency policy. For each timelog to remove, confirm that the current timesheet actually includes it.

Perform the update in a single transaction: load the existing join rows for the timesheet, insert new join rows for added timelogs, and delete or mark inactive the join rows for removed timelogs according to the join-table lifecycle used by the service layer. Recompute any derived totals required for the response, such as included timelog count and summed duration if the timesheet response schema exposes them. If the timesheet transitions or lock behavior requires it, ensure no approved-state invariants are broken.

Return the refreshed timesheet aggregate with its current timelog links. Include clear validation failures for cases such as non-draft timesheet, cross-employee timelog, timelog outside the week range, timelog already assigned to another timesheet, or permission denial. Never mutate the underlying timelog fact records during this operation.

responseBody.description: Paginated updated timesheets after timelog membership changes.

requestBody.description: Timelog add/remove instructions for the draft timesheet.

operations.description:
Submit a draft timesheet for approval.

This operation moves a weekly timesheet from draft status into submitted status for the currently selected organization context. It is part of the employee self-service workflow for weekly time collection and is only available for the employee who owns the timesheet. Once submitted, the timesheet becomes available for review by users who have timesheet approval permission.

The submission is allowed only when the timesheet contains at least one timelog. The system must reject submission when the timesheet has no timelogs, when the timesheet is not in draft status, or when another timesheet for the same employee and the same week is already submitted or approved. These rules ensure that one employee cannot create overlapping weekly submissions and that approvers only review complete weekly records.

A successful submission updates the timesheet lifecycle state and preserves the employee-week association in the organization boundary. The operation does not edit timelog content directly; it only validates the current draft, records the submitted state, and makes the record available for approval or rejection through the timesheet review workflow.
operations.name: process
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by timesheetId within the authenticated member's selected organization context. Verify that the timesheet exists, belongs to the employee associated with the authenticated member, and is in draft status.

Before transitioning state, count or otherwise verify that the timesheet has at least one associated timelog through the timesheet-timelog relation. Reject with a domain validation error if the collection is empty.

Check for conflicting timesheets for the same employee and the same week where status is submitted or approved. If any such record exists, reject the request to prevent duplicate weekly submissions.

If all validations pass, update the timesheet status to submitted in a single transaction. Preserve the existing employee, organization, and week fields, and keep any linked timelogs associated with the timesheet. Return the updated timesheet entity after commit.

Authorization must ensure the caller is the employee owner of the timesheet, not merely any member of the organization. Approver permissions are not required for this action.

Handle error cases with clear business responses: not found when the timesheet does not belong to the current context, forbidden when the caller is not the owner, conflict when another submitted or approved timesheet exists for the same employee-week, and unprocessable entity when there are no timelogs or the status is not draft.

responseBody.description: The submitted timesheet after the status transition.

operations.description:
Approve a submitted weekly timesheet and finalize its review outcome.

This operation is used by an authorized reviewer to accept a timesheet that has already been submitted for approval within the current organization context. A timesheet may only be approved while it is in submitted status, and the approval decision becomes part of the employee’s weekly time tracking history as well as the organization’s activity record.

When the approval succeeds, the timesheet enters the approved state and the timelogs included in that timesheet become locked from further edit or deletion through the timesheet workflow. This preserves the reviewed weekly time record and prevents later changes from altering the approved hours. The approved timesheet remains available as a completed review record for both the employee and the approver.
